text:
Dear @Somnath_Temple Management Team,
Having attended several online pujas, I would like to offer a few suggestions.

1. Booking Process
Bulk & Recurring Bookings: Just as you offer multiple options for Bilva Puja during Shravan, pls extend this to other pujas like Rudrabhishek. Ideally, allow to book for multiple days & pujas in a single transaction rather than repeating the process.
Family Inclusion: Allow to add multiple family members & select multiple pujas under one booking.
Slot Preference: Allow to select preferred time slots during the booking process. This will ensure working professionals can plan ahead & not miss their Sankalp puja.

2. Hindu Calendar
Pls upload the temple’s official Hindu calendar on the website so people can easily track tithis; especially useful during overlapping or double tithis.

3. Birthday Puja
Birth Tithi: The free birthday puja is indeed a wonderful gesture, but people naturally add the Gregorian date. It would be great if people could add birth tithi.
Advance Guidelines: Pls share the dos & don'ts for birthday puja (or any other puja) in the booking email (as well as mention water for Sankalp). No point saying it when people have already joined streaming.
Seamless Transition: Pls try to remove the 15-20 min gap between the Sankalp & the Garbh Griha puja. Sitting cross-legged for long periods is not easy for many, making them to log out before the latter begins.

4. Pitru Puja Option
Pls introduce a distinct category for Pitru puja. Since the note section was removed from the booking form, there is no way to specify this intention.

5. Gaushala Donations
Allow flexible donation amounts for Gaushala instead of a fixed INR 1,100; it encourages more people to contribute what they can.

6. Bhojanalaya Terminology
Consider replacing Smriti & Tithi with straightforward labels such as Birthday, Anniversary, Auspicious Day & Pitru Tithi.

7. Broadcast Link
Consider setting up a one-way broadcast link for online pujas instead of Zoom links. This would prevent disruptions caused by participants' unmuted microphones, videos, or chats, offering a much more peaceful experience.

Jai Somnath 🙏

text:
On 15th September 1944, Esteri Kokundeka went into labour. Like every mother welcoming a child into the world, she could not have known the full weight of the journey ahead, that the young boy she brought forth would one day carry upon his shoulders questions of war and peace, liberation and reconstruction, leadership and the future of a nation.

That boy was Yoweri Kaguta Museveni.

His story would grow beyond the boundaries of his home. Education sharpened his intellect; the politics of his generation awakened his consciousness; and his involvement in youth movements cultivated an enduring conviction that political independence without socioeconomic transformation would remain incomplete.

Then came exile.

Around 1972, in Tanzania, FRONASA emerged as part of the struggle against dictatorship. These were dangerous years. Behind the revolutionary was also a husband and father whose young family lived with the uncertainty of whether he would return from the dangerous missions he carried out.

He could have chosen the relative comfort of exile. An intellectual young man could have pursued a life elsewhere. But there are moments when intellect demands responsibility. He chose to lead the struggle for his homeland, seemingly persuaded that no individual family could be truly secure while the larger national family remained insecure.

@KagutaMuseveni and FRONASA highly involed, Idi Amin fell in 1979. The disputed elections of 1980 followed, and Mr. Museveni chose another difficult road, the five-year armed struggle that eventually brought the National Resistance Army to Kampala.

Then came 26th January 1986.

I often reflect on the metaphor of “encwacure”, the orphaned, malnourished calf.

The NRA inherited a country weakened by years of political upheaval, institutional breakdown, economic distress and conflict. The task before the new leadership was therefore not simply to govern; it was to nurse a wounded state back towards stability.

For forty years, that calf has been fed, treated, protected and allowed to grow.

Today, the calf is no longer what it was.

It has grown into a strong cow, healthier, more confident and capable of producing milk and giving birth to new calves. 

Uganda still has challenges, as every living nation does, but the distance travelled matters. Nations, like people, must sometimes be understood not only by where they stand, but also by where they started, what they survived and what they have built along the way. It because of that therefore that I despise the comparison of Uganda to other countries before the honest comparison of Uganda Now to Uganda then.

Perhaps one of President Museveni’s most consequential legacies is not simply the number of years he has led, but the people he has groomed along the journey. Across government, security, diplomacy, business, academia and public service are generations of men and women who have passed through his school of leadership.

Leadership, after all, is not merely occupying the driver’s seat. It is developing people who can understand the road.

As I celebrate H.E. President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni on his birthday today, I reflect not merely on the President, but on the long journey of the student activist, the revolutionary, the exile, the soldier, the statesman, the father, grandfather, and the political thinker.

History will continue to interrogate every era, as it should. But history must also remember the roads travelled, the sacrifices made and the difficult decisions taken when the destination was far from certain.

It is 82 years of a purposeful life lived, From the young man who believed in socioeconomic transformation, to the revolutionary who chose home when exile offered another life, to the leader who inherited encwacure and spent decades nurturing it, the journey itself carries lessons about conviction, patience, organisation, resilience and strategic leadership.

text:
20 Famous Places in Morocco You Should Visit at Least Once
Morocco is a country of incredible contrasts from ancient medinas and colorful souks to Atlantic beaches, dramatic mountains, historic kasbahs, and the golden dunes of the Sahara Desert.

If you are planning a Morocco trip, this map highlights 20 famous places in Morocco that deserve a place on your travel list.

Here are some of the destinations and landmarks to discover:

1. Marrakech — Explore the historic Medina, Jemaa el-Fna, Bahia Palace, and Majorelle Garden.

2. Fes — Discover one of Morocco’s most fascinating ancient medinas and its rich cultural heritage.

3. Chefchaouen — Wander through the famous blue-painted streets of Morocco’s Rif Mountains.

4. Casablanca — Visit the impressive Hassan II Mosque and experience Morocco’s modern coastal city.

5. Rabat — Discover Morocco’s capital, including the Kasbah of the Udayas and historic monuments.

6. Meknes — Explore one of Morocco’s historic Imperial Cities and its impressive old medina.

7. Essaouira — Enjoy the relaxed Atlantic atmosphere, historic harbor, medina, and coastal scenery.

8. Tangier — Discover the city where the Mediterranean meets the Atlantic, with a fascinating international history.

9. Merzouga & Erg Chebbi — Experience the Sahara Desert, camel rides, spectacular sunsets, and nights beneath the stars.

10. Erg Chigaga — Travel deeper into the Sahara for a more remote desert experience surrounded by vast sand dunes.

11. Ait Ben Haddou — Visit the famous UNESCO-listed ksar and one of southern Morocco’s most iconic landscapes.

12. Ouarzazate — Explore the gateway to the Moroccan Sahara and the landscapes famous from cinema and television.

13. Dades Valley — Discover dramatic rock formations, green valleys, and traditional villages along the Road of a Thousand Kasbahs.

14. Todra Gorge — Walk between spectacular limestone cliffs in one of Morocco’s most impressive natural landscapes.

15. Atlas Mountains — Experience mountain villages, valleys, panoramic landscapes, and traditional Amazigh culture.

16. Volubilis — Step into Morocco’s Roman past among remarkably preserved ancient ruins.

17. El Jadida — Discover the historic Portuguese city and its atmospheric old quarter on Morocco’s Atlantic coast.

18. Ifrane — See a completely different side of Morocco in this mountain town surrounded by cedar forests.

19. Agafay Desert — Enjoy a desert escape close to Marrakech, with rocky landscapes, sunset experiences, and desert camps.

From Marrakech to Fes, Chefchaouen to Essaouira, the Atlas Mountains to the Sahara Desert, Morocco offers something for almost every type of traveler.

Which of these 20 famous places in Morocco would you visit first?

Tell us in the comments and if you have already visited Morocco, which destination would you add to this map?

If you are planning a private Morocco tour, Deep Morocco Tours can help create a tailor-made itinerary based on your interests, travel style, and the amount of time you have in Morocco.

text:
Kennedy center near bankruptcy without Trump’s name on facade – WaPo
The Washington arts institution is reportedly nearing “fiscal collapse” after ticket sales and fundraising plunged, while its main building may also be unsafe
Published 14 Sep, 2026 (FULL)
https://t.co/jz73AWz7mb
Washington’s Kennedy Center is reportedly on the brink of bankruptcy after ticket sales and fundraising plunged in recent months, the Washington Post said on Monday. The re-inscription of US President Donald Trump’s name on the building is being considered as a possible solution.
After returning to office, Trump overhauled the board of trustees of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts – Washington’s flagship national arts venue and a memorial to the assassinated US president. He also appointed himself chairman.
Last December, his name was added to the facade of the building but was met with protests, legal challenges, and a backlash among performers and audiences. The inscription was taken down after a US District Judge ruled in May that only Congress could change the building’s name and ordered the signage removed.
According to documents obtained by the Washington Post, the Kennedy Center now faces “certain fiscal collapse” within weeks. Internal forecasts cited by the outlet showed revenue has fallen far below target, leaving the institution with a multimillion-dollar deficit despite major spending cuts.
The center’s board has been told that Trump has offered to help raise enough money to prevent bankruptcy. However, he is reportedly unwilling to provide the necessary fundraising and oversight without “appropriate recognition” for his role.
Trustees will consider several inscriptions on Tuesday, including one stating that the center’s renovation, restoration, and endowment were overseen by Trump and the “Trump Kennedy Center Fund.”
The financial black hole is not the center’s only problem. Management is also urging trustees to close the main building immediately, saying it is unsafe for continued use after a large section of ceiling plaster crashed down inside the Grand Foyer during a storm.
Engineers have also found widespread corrosion in parts of the structure, including in heavy ceiling assemblies hanging above public walkways. The board had already approved a two-year renovation, but officials now say the main venue may need to shut as early as Tuesday.
Trump’s push to put his name on the Kennedy Center comes as part of a broader rebranding campaign that has already included the renaming of a federal peace institute, a prescription-drug website, a visa program, a planned class of US Navy battleships, and a stretch of road near his Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida.
Democratic senators have responded with the Stop Executive Renaming for Vanity and Ego, or SERVE Act, which if passed would bar federal property from being named after a sitting president.

🇸🇦🪳|The Saudi-Israeli-CENTCOM Intelligence Axis: An Arab kingdom, facing incoming missiles, turned to a nation it had never recognized to request intelligence.

On September 15, 2026, news emerged from Middle Eastern diplomatic circles, news deliberately downplayed by mainstream Western media but simultaneously confirmed by both Arab and Israeli outlets:

Saudi Arabia and Israel held talks on intelligence cooperation, mediated by US Central Command (CENTCOM).

Saudi Arabia an Arab kingdom that has never established formal diplomatic relations with Israel and has publicly insisted that "normalization with Israel will not occur until a Palestinian state is established" requested intelligence support from Israel via CENTCOM.

This was not a "strategic partnership." It was a "wartime plea for help." And the party Saudi Arabia turned to for help was a nation it had never recognized.

🎯The reason Saudi Arabia turned to Israel was not a "shared threat from Iran." It was two refusals from the United States.

On September 10, 2026, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump twice, requesting that the US launch direct military strikes against Yemeni armed forces. Trump refused both times. Washington’s directive was clear: concentrate US forces on Iran and the Strait of Hormuz, and do not open a new front in Yemen.

The US was willing only to provide intelligence and targeting data. Approximately 200 US military personnel were stationed in Saudi Arabia to provide "non-kinetic support."

What Saudi Arabia needed was fighter jets, missiles, and air support. What the US offered was "intelligence."

So, Saudi Arabia turned to Israel.

Israel possessed something Saudi Arabia lacked: real-world intelligence capabilities regarding the Yemen theater of operations. The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) had already demonstrated intelligence and operational capabilities in the waters surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, helping the US build a multi-layered intelligence picture of Iranian military positions.

The intelligence support requested by Saudi Arabia focused on constructing a more comprehensive picture of the Yemeni armed forces' military deployments and identifying potential plans for their future operations.  Translation: Saudi Arabia wanted to know the locations of the Yemeni armed forces' missile launchers, drone bases, and command centers. Israel knew the answers.

💀CENTCOM’s role in this matter was not that of a "neutral mediator." Rather, having declined to engage in direct combat, the U.S. positioned CENTCOM as a "substitute security provider" for Saudi Arabia.

CENTCOM Commander Vice Admiral Brad Cooper flew to Saudi Arabia on September 10 for urgent consultations with Saudi officials. His mission was not to "help Saudi Arabia fight," but to assess the situation and coordinate existing U.S. assistance.

However, the assistance the U.S. could provide was limited. The U.S. would not deploy fighter jets, launch missiles, or intercept the Yemeni armed forces' drones.

Consequently, CENTCOM did the only thing it could: it integrated Israel’s intelligence capabilities into Saudi Arabia’s security framework.

This was not "mediation"; it was "outsourcing." The U.S. outsourced security capabilities which it was either unable or unwilling to provide itself to Israel. CENTCOM served as the executor of this outsourcing chain.

🕵️Israel’s intelligence capabilities regarding Yemen were not built overnight.

In March 2026, Israel announced the establishment of a military base in Somaliland to gather intelligence on the Yemeni armed forces and conduct operations against them. An Israeli general revealed to Bloomberg that Israel had set up a special intelligence unit targeting the Yemeni armed forces, as the group possessed hundreds of rockets capable of striking Israel.

Israeli intelligence agencies Aman (Military Intelligence) and Mossad maintained intelligence assets operating directly within Yemen. In April 2026, the Yemeni armed forces announced the dismantling of a spy network linked to Israeli intelligence, arresting multiple individuals who had collaborated directly with Aman, Mossad, and other agencies.

This meant that Israel had "insiders" within the Yemeni armed forces. Israel knew what the Yemeni armed forces were doing, what they were preparing to do, and where they were doing it.

This was precisely what Saudi Arabia needed. While Saudi Arabia possessed satellites and drones, it lacked human intelligence (HUMINT) from within the Yemeni armed forces. Israel had it.  

🇬🇧Saudi Arabia didn't just turn to Israel for help; it also made a request to the UK.

Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia asked the UK for assistance in repelling the Yemeni armed forces from the Bab al-Mandab Strait and protecting Saudi oil infrastructure. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham agreed to send British military advisors but did not commit to providing any additional military support.

"Military advisors." Not fighter jets. Not air defense systems. Not missiles.

The UK is doing the same thing as the US: providing advisors, not combat forces.

In the span of just one week, Saudi Arabia simultaneously appealed to the US, Israel, and the UK for help. The response it received consisted of: 200 US troops providing intelligence, some intelligence sharing from Israel, and a few British advisors.

Meanwhile, missiles from the Yemeni armed forces are striking Saudi cities.

🔄 At the same time Saudi Arabia was requesting intelligence from Israel via CENTCOM, Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan spoke by phone with Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi. The two sides discussed "growing insecurity" and "emphasized the need for continued cooperation and diplomatic efforts to prevent the spread of tensions."

Saudi Arabia is doing two things at once:

◾ Requesting intelligence from Israel to use against the Yemeni armed forces.
◾ Calling Iran to discuss "preventing the spread of tensions."

This isn't "playing both sides." It is a "survival strategy." Saudi Arabia knows that Israeli intelligence can help it locate targets, but it also knows that Israeli intelligence cannot stop the Yemeni armed forces' missiles. Saudi Arabia needs Iran, the primary backer of the Yemeni armed forces to facilitate some form of de-escalation.

But Iran's conditions are clear. In the September 10th call, and throughout the war, Iran has consistently maintained that an end to the aggression against and blockade of Yemen is a prerequisite for any negotiations.

Saudi Arabia is moving forward on two tracks simultaneously: one leading to Israeli intelligence, the other to Iranian diplomacy. And these two tracks will ultimately converge on the battlefield in Yemen.

🛢️ The timing of Saudi Arabia’s pivot toward Israel reveals its true fear.

On September 11, Yemeni armed forces secured full control over the area surrounding the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, seizing Perim Island (Mayyun), Zuqar Island, and the Hanish Islands. Officials from the Yemeni government forces admitted that Saudi-backed troops had "collapsed" and that the Yemeni armed forces had "completed their takeover of the Bab el-Mandeb region and Perim Island."

Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline.the only alternative route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz was forced to partially shut down following a drone attack. Inventories at the port of Yanbu were sufficient for only five to seven days of exports. Saudi oil tankers were forced to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope, extending the voyage from four days to thirty-four.

Saudi Arabia’s two oil export chokepoints the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb Strait are simultaneously being throttled by resistance forces.

Yet the Saudi military, having fought in Yemen for twelve years and possessing state-of-the-art U.S. weaponry, has been unable to prevent a force lacking an air force from seizing control of the Bab el-Mandeb Strait.

What Saudi Arabia needs is not "more weapons." It needs "better intelligence." And Israel happens to possess exactly that.

📢BREAKING: The US just publicly admitted it has weapons in orbit 

Not "developing" Not "studying" Deployed! Right now - Confirmed! 🇺🇸🛰️

For years Washington's position was: "China and Russia are weaponizing space. We would never" 🤞

Yesterday, Air Force Secretary Troy Meink stood up in front of the defense press and declared:

"The United States now has on-orbit space control weapons capable of defending the joint force"

No details on what they are. No details on how many. No details on when they got there. Just... trust us, they're defensive 🎪

Defensive is doing galaxy-sized lifting here...

Three things worth knowing:

1️⃣ The Space Force's own follow-up killed the "defensive" framing. A spokesperson confirmed these systems cover "disruption, degradation and even destruction" — for "offensive AND defensive purposes at the direction of combatant commands"

That's not a shield. That's a loaded gun over everyone's head

2️⃣ The same speech announced Golden Dome's space-based interceptor hardware is "flight ready" — with the first targeting satellites launching this month and a 2028 constellation. A system the CBO thinks could cost $1.2 TRILLION over 20 years

You don't announce you have orbital weapons while asking Congress for a trillion-dollar orbital weapons program by accident. This disclosure is a also a budget request

3️⃣ The legal farce: the same Pentagon that spent years lecturing other nations and the UN about "responsible behavior in space" and pushing a ban on destructive anti-satellite tests. And no, it's not illegal. 

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty bans nukes in orbit — not conventional weapons. Washington just proved it wrote that loophole for itself sixty years ago. All that hand-wringing about "responsible behavior in space"? The US championed a destructive ASAT test ban... right up until it needed orbital weapons to sell a missile shield

But here's what they're NOT telling you:

The US and Russia already keep nuclear forces on hair-trigger alert. China does not. That's been one of the few stabilizing factors in nuclear strategy!

China holds a No First Use nuclear policy. Russia and North Korea don't. What message does the US just send China by confirming — publicly — that American weapons sitting over Chinese territory can blind, jam, or destroy the satellites that feed China's nuclear warning and command systems?

Think like Beijing for one minute. Hunter satellites over your head. Interceptors going up in 2028. A trillion-dollar shield whose only strategic purpose is making China believe its deterrent might not survive

You don't need to abandon No First Use on paper to harden it in practice. Disperse. Raise readiness. Move faster. The threshold shifts even if the doctrine doesn't. That is exactly how nuclear states end up at launch-on-warning hair-triggers — not by declaration, but by pressure⚠️

And Pyongyang? Kim Jong Un, North Korea's leader  just stated during a party congress that he wants "special assets for attacking adversary satellites" Washington just handed him the justification on a silver platter. A cheap nuclear DA-ASAT is the budget answer to a trillion-dollar dome. Watch that space. Literally...

Meanwhile — in typical US hypocritical fashion  — Meink's reasoning for going public was that US weapons "offer a deterrence capability" because Beijing and Moscow did it first 🤥

Citation: classified

But now that the Americans have CONFIRMED their orbital weapons, the next public admission from China or Russia that they decide to place weapons in orbit will be called "proof of escalation"

That's not strategy. That's the oldest trick in the imperial handbook: break the rule loudly, then lecture everyone else I told you so

For sixty years the whole space arms control architecture rested on one polite norm, not to militarize space

Washington just broke the taboo and stepped on the accelerator

Space is no longer a sanctuary. It is now a warfighting domain. And the infrastructure of modern civilization — GPS, banking, communications, weather forecasting — sits directly in the crossfire

For decades, we treated satellites as reliable, neutral, almost invisible infrastructure. That era is over!

Pandora's box just achieved orbital velocity. The only question now is how many countries will dragged down with it 🌏💥

text:
Experts verklaren dat Oekraïne zijn technologische voorsprong verliest door baanbrekende Russische innovatie https://t.co/5nbKGNf1Bt via @Frontnieuws 

Er doen twee oogopenende artikelen de ronde over Oekraïne, die de steeds somberder wordende stemming achter de schermen bij vooraanstaande denkers en besluitvormers blootleggen met betrekking tot de huidige situatie en de toekomstperspectieven van Oekraïne.

Opgemerkt moet worden dat de mainstream media steeds ongezouten zijn in hun beoordelingen, zoals blijkt uit verschillende recente artikelen waarin wordt opgeroepen tot “eerlijkheid“ in de westerse dialoog over de werkelijke toestand van Oekraïne, schrijft Simplicius.

Het probleem is dat eerlijkheid moet uitgaan van de eerste principes: dit betekent dat de meest elementaire, fundamentele en cruciale feiten van een bepaald scenario moeten worden vastgesteld. In het geval van Oekraïne zou een beoordeling op basis van de eerste principes moeten voortvloeien uit de fundamentele, kwantificeerbare oorlogskosten, met als belangrijkste factor het aantal slachtoffers. Als het Westen niet in staat is om eerlijk de werkelijke verliezen van Oekraïne onder de loep te nemen, op dezelfde manier als het dat wekelijks doet voor die van Rusland, dan zal het nooit de waarheid van de situatie benaderen. Dat komt omdat vrijwel alle huidige problemen van Oekraïne voortkomen uit het enorme aantal slachtoffers, en dat is de meest essentiële olifant in de kamer die het Westen op flagrante wijze blijft negeren.

Nu over naar de artikelen.

Het eerste artikel uit The Spectator doet een gewaagde uitspraak:
https://t.co/ZwAMDevZXk

Het artikel begint met drie “deprimerende conclusies“ in de nasleep van het laatste zinloze diplomatieke pingpongspel van Kushner en Witkoff:

Vladimir Poetin heeft zijn oorlogsdoelen sinds 2022 geen jota gewijzigd en blijft vastbesloten om door te vechten. Donald Trump heeft geen nieuw vredesplan, behalve het beëindigen van de oorlog in Oekraïne op de voorwaarden van Poetin. En Kiev raakt zonder geld en manschappen om zich te verdedigen, net zo zeker als het al zonder Patriot-raketten zit om zijn luchtruim te verdedigen tegen de spervuuraanvallen van het Kremlin.

Dat zijn de drie deprimerende conclusies uit de laatste ronde van pendeldiplomatie in Moskou en Kiev door Trumps schoonzoon Jared Kushner en speciaal gezant Steve Witkoff.

De auteur zet de sombere toon van zijn analyse voort bij het beschrijven van het groeiende overwicht van Rusland op het slagveld, dat later een sleutelrol zal spelen in onze interpretatie:

Wat nog belangrijker is: terwijl het Kremlin zijn meedogenloze campagne voortzet om de Oekraïense steden onleefbaar te maken, de economie van het land te vernietigen en het van zijn toekomst te beroven, wordt het vermogen van Kiev om zich te verdedigen ernstig in twijfel getrokken.

Een deel van de zich ontvouwende nachtmerrie van Oekraïne is tactisch van aard. Elk van de Russische langeafstandsaanvalssystemen is verwoestender geworden. Een nieuwe generatie Geran-aanvalsdrones met straalmotor, die veel sneller en nauwkeuriger zijn dan hun oude Iraanse Shahed-modellen, wordt massaal ingezet. Rusland ontwikkelt ten minste twee nieuwe, goedkope kruisraketsystemen en voert de productie van vanuit de lucht en vanaf de grond gelanceerde ballistische raketten op. “Dit is een oorlog tegen steden en infrastructuur. Niemand zal deze winnen,” zei Serhii Beskrestnov, adviseur van Zelensky op het gebied van defensietechnologieën en een vooraanstaand figuur binnen het defensieapparaat van Kiev, dit weekend tegen The Guardian. “De aanval is sterker geworden dan de verdediging.” Beskrestnov voorspelt dat Oekraïne deze winter niet in staat zal zijn om voldoende raketten te verkrijgen om de Oekraïense steden volledig tegen verwoesting te beschermen.

Het artikel biedt verrassend veel inzicht door de eerlijke analyse van de talloze manieren waarop Oekraïne de oorlog aan het verliezen is:

Maar een groter deel van de zich langzaam ontvouwende nederlaag van Oekraïne is strategisch van aard…

…de derde en ernstigste mislukking is de weigering om serieus vredesbesprekingen met het Kremlin aan te gaan, en de hardnekkige overtuiging dat het aanmoedigen van Oekraïne om te blijven vechten – en voor altijd te blijven vechten – op de een of andere manier op magische wijze tot overwinning zal leiden.

Het belangrijkste is dat de auteur wijst op de naderende begrotingsramp in Oekraïne, nu de Europese bereidheid voor nog meer eindeloze leningen is opgedroogd:
  De Russische oorlogsstrategie is totaal anders dan wij denken

Het kritieke punt – waarop die beloften uiteindelijk hard met de realiteit zullen botsen – zal zich binnenkort voordoen in de vorm van een dreigende begrotingscrisis in Kiev. De Oekraïense premier Serhii Koretsky heeft onlangs aangekondigd dat Kiev het grootste deel van zijn defensiemiddelen voor 2026 al heeft uitgegeven en geconfronteerd wordt met een dreigend begrotingstekort van 26 miljard euro (30 miljard dollar) – ondanks een recente lening van 90 miljard euro (104 miljard dollar) van de EU. Die lening, die na maandenlang gekonkel in Brussel werd veiliggesteld, vertegenwoordigde het hoogtepunt van wat de EU realistisch gezien in staat is bijeen te brengen. Nu Oekraïne de zwaarste en meest slopende winter van de oorlog tegemoet gaat, raakt het niet alleen de Patriot-raketten en manschappen voor de frontlinies kwijt, maar ook het geld om door te vechten.

Een goed voorbeeld hiervan:
https://t.co/qZxbkeOUXl

De slotzin van de auteur is zijn meest eerlijke en realistische – in plaats van stiekem op te roepen tot meer wapens en eindeloze escalatie, zoals de meeste van dit soort artikelen in hun slotparagrafen doen, geeft deze auteur toe dat diplomatieke gesprekken met Rusland het enige zijn dat Oekraïne nog kan redden, waarbij hij terecht opmerkt dat elk vredesvoorstel steeds slechter is geworden:

Wat kan Oekraïne redden van politieke en militaire ineenstorting? Er zijn tekenen dat het politieke taboe in Europa om met Poetin te praten aan het afbrokkelen is. Alice Weidel van de Duitse AfD, die onlangs de verkiezingen in Saksen heeft gewonnen, heeft opgeroepen tot “een open kanaal naar Rusland om tot een akkoord te komen en een vreedzame oplossing te bereiken“. Volgens Iuliia Mendel, de perssecretaris van Zelensky van 2019 tot 2021, “komen er nieuwe krachten op, en die worden steeds sterker“, die “onze enige kans op een vreedzaam Europa“ vertegenwoordigen… Meer wapens zullen ons niet redden. Dat hebben ze nooit gedaan.”

Tot nu toe is elk volgend vredesvoorstel voor Kiev slechter geweest dan het vorige. Het lijkt erop dat Poetins duidelijke bedoeling is om de Oekraïense steden nog een brute laatste klap toe te dienen, voordat hij de oorlog uiteindelijk op zijn eigen voorwaarden beëindigt, wellicht volgend jaar. De regering-Trump heeft het idee om een volledige Oekraïense overwinning te steunen al lang opgegeven, en het is aan historici om te beoordelen of dat besluit om Amerikaanse hulp en wapens in te trekken een zelfvervullende profetie is geworden. Europa blijft van zijn kant mooie woorden spreken. Maar het heeft geen concreet plan om Oekraïne te helpen of te redden van de woede van het Kremlin – laat staan om de Russische economie te verpletteren of Poetins wil te breken.

Dit brengt ons bij het volgende en meest ingrijpende artikel, compleet met twee alternatieve koppen:
https://t.co/MA41ZXeEBX

Het is geschreven voor de Washington Post door voormalig Google-topman Eric Schmidt, die een tweede, heroplevende carrière heeft als zowel organisator als ondernemer op het gebied van anti-Russische oorlogstechnologie. In de nasleep van een recente reis naar Kiev is Schmidts beoordeling somberder dan ooit:

Ik ben tijdens de hele lange oorlog met Rusland naar Oekraïne gereisd om het Oekraïense leger te helpen bij de ontwikkeling van geavanceerde technologieën voor het slagveld. Maar ik kwam terug van deze meest recente reis met meer zorgen dan ooit sinds de allereerste dagen van de invasie.

Vervolgens beschrijft hij nuchter hoe Rusland een cruciale technologische superioriteit ten opzichte van Oekraïne aan het verwerven is door een grootschalige oorlogsindustrialisatie op gang te brengen die alleen door het hele Westen samen kan worden geëvenaard:

Rusland wordt steeds beter in het voeren van dit conflict, en Washington moet erkennen dat het afstevent op een strategie van totale oorlog, waarbij het zijn fabrieken en mankracht mobiliseert om Oekraïne tot overgave te bombarderen. Om Rusland te verslaan is nu meer nodig dan alleen de levering van wapens. Oekraïne zal het Westen nodig hebben om zijn collectieve middelen in te zetten op een schaal die groot genoeg is om de vijand qua productie te overtreffen en het langer vol te houden dan de vijand.

Oekraïne had lange tijd een asymmetrisch voordeel, schrijft hij. Terwijl Rusland zich richtte op “industriële massa“, d.w.z. kwantiteit boven kwaliteit, zette Oekraïne innovatie in als tegenkracht. Nu, zegt hij, heeft Rusland een sprong voorwaarts gemaakt in beide categorieën: een ongekende schaal van productie in combinatie met bliksemsnelle innovatie die Oekraïne in puin achterlaat:
  Als AI beslist wie er sterft: de eerste moorddrones hebben blijkbaar al mensen gedood

Dat voordeel neemt snel af. Toen Oekraïne onderscheppingsraketten ontwikkelde die de zwermen Shahed-drones van Rusland konden vernietigen, paste Rusland zich aan en zette snellere, door straalmotoren aangedreven Shaheds in die veel moeilijker te onderscheppen zijn. Rusland is bezig met het inzetten van een satellietconstellatie die Starlink moet evenaren, een systeem dat Oekraïense drone-eenheden gebruiken om Russische troepen in het bezette Oekraïne aan te vallen. Jarenlang bestond de strategie van het Kremlin uit het inzetten van industriële massa tegen Oekraïense innovatie, maar nu combineert het die massa met zijn eigen innovaties.

Interessant genoeg draait zijn artikel om het thema “de winter overleven”. Oekraïne heeft hulp nodig, nu de meest meedogenloze winter van de oorlog snel nadert. De draden worden voor ons aan elkaar geknoopt: het establishment is zich ervan bewust geworden dat Oekraïne, bloedend, wankelend en krap bij kas, deze winter op zijn laatste benen zal lopen.
https://t.co/1W9e5jcXyZ

In het artikel van Reuters staat dat de sluiting van de havens van Odessa door Rusland de Oekraïense begroting in een neerwaartse spiraal brengt.

[Roksolana Pidlasa, voorzitter van de parlementaire begrotingscommissie] zei dat de oorlog steeds duurder wordt en dat Oekraïne zijn defensiebehoeften niet langer volledig uit binnenlandse middelen kan financieren, zoals in voorgaande jaren het geval was.

Nu heeft Rusland de grensovergangen van Oekraïne naar Roemenië en Moldavië aangevallen. De grenspost bij Orlovka naar Roemenië werd begin september aangevallen, terwijl de grenspost bij Starokazachye naar Moldavië in de nacht van 9 september werd aangevallen:
https://t.co/IkLw9Tw5H0

Deze grensovergangen werden door Oekraïne gebruikt als landroute om zijn graan te vervoeren nadat de graanterminals in Odessa waren uitgeschakeld. Maar nu worden zelfs deze routes door Rusland geblokkeerd, waardoor Oekraïne op een cruciaal moment de broodnodige inkomsten worden ontzegd.

Het overheersende thema in de bovengenoemde berichten, waaronder dat van Eric Schmidt, is hoe Rusland zich aanpast en innoveert, met name door het gebruik van een nieuwe generatie drones die de Oekraïense luchtverdediging in de war brengen en die deze niet kan bijhouden:
https://t.co/QKorbWqv0o

Het bovenstaande FT-verslag richt zich op de nieuwste Russische, door straalmotoren aangedreven Gerans, de -4- en -5-serie:

De nieuwe, door straalmotoren aangedreven Geran-4- en Geran-5-drones van Rusland hebben de afgelopen weken Oekraïense steden zwaar getroffen en ontwijken de luchtverdediging in veel grotere mate dan hun door propellers aangedreven voorgangers, waardoor ze een grote nieuwe bedreiging vormen.

Het is een opvallende verschuiving voor een leger waarvan de successen op het slagveld sinds de invasie van Vladimir Poetin in 2022 gepaard zijn gegaan met enorme menselijke offers en zware verliezen aan materieel uit het Sovjettijdperk. Terwijl Oekraïne uitblinkt in eigen ontwikkelde innovaties op het gebied van defensietechnologie, tonen de nieuwe drones aan dat Rusland ook in staat is om op grote schaal nieuwe wapens te ontwikkelen, te verfijnen en in te zetten, aldus deskundigen.

Een van de onthullingen uit het rapport die viraal is gegaan, is dat de Russische ontwikkelingen op het gebied van deze drones ertoe hebben geleid dat Iran grote belangstelling heeft getoond voor de aanschaf van de nieuwste varianten voor eigen gebruik:

De Russische dronecapaciteiten zijn zo sterk verbeterd dat Teheran Moskou dit jaar heeft gevraagd om geavanceerde Geran-drones voor gebruik in zijn oorlog met Israël en de VS, aldus westerse veiligheidsfunctionarissen en een persoon die dicht bij het Kremlin staat.

Met name de mobiele vuurteams van Oekraïne hebben grote moeite om deze drones bij te houden. Voorheen werden de langzaam vliegende, door propellers aangedreven Gerans opgemerkt door radars en andere vroegtijdige waarschuwingssystemen, waardoor mobiele vuurteams in “technische“ pick-uptrucks snel naar een onderscheppingspunt in de vliegroute van de drone konden rijden. Maar de straaldrones maken dit nu onmogelijk, aangezien civiele grondvoertuigen simpelweg niet snel genoeg kunnen rijden om de vliegroutes van de drones te onderscheppen.
  Paul Craig Roberts: Militaristische onzin

Oekraïne onderschept slechts ongeveer 60 procent van de straaldrijvende drones, vergeleken met de 90 tot 95 procent die het land routinematig haalt tegen andere versies, aldus luchtmachtwoordvoerder Yuriy Ihnat.

“Binnenkort zullen we waarschijnlijk zien dat deze drones over stealth-capaciteiten beschikken, en dat betekent dat het nog duurder wordt om ze te produceren, aan te schaffen en te gebruiken, maar ook om ze te vernietigen,” zei hij.

Zodra deze drones worden gekoppeld aan het Russische “Starlink“-systeem, genaamd “Rassvet“, dat momenteel wordt ingezet, zal dit een geheel nieuw, onoverkomelijk probleem vormen voor Oekraïne, met name in de uiterst westelijke regio’s die tot nu toe relatieve veiligheid genoten in het beschermde “achterland“.

Een vooraanstaande Oekraïense commandant baarde onlangs opzien door toe te geven dat dit volgend jaar zal leiden tot de totale nederlaag van Oekraïne:

BREAKING: “Rusland zal binnen een jaar satellietcommunicatie hebben over het gehele grondgebied van Oekraïne, en dit zal leiden tot onze nederlaag,“ aldus de commandant van het 1e Aanvalsbataljon van de Oekraïense strijdkrachten, ”Perun”.

Een vooraanstaande Oekraïense analist geeft een eveneens pessimistische inschatting:

Tatarigami_UA @Tatarigami_UA · 12 sep.

Ons team bij Frontelligence Insight merkt op dat de Russische industrie Oekraïne niet alleen op verschillende gebieden van de droneproductie heeft ingehaald, vaak door simpelweg bestaande producten te kopiëren, maar ook een voorsprong heeft genomen bij het opschalen van de productie. Dit omvat gedecentraliseerde productienetwerken waarbij tientallen bedrijven in de hele toeleveringsketen betrokken zijn.

Deze trend is niet dit jaar begonnen, maar de cumulatieve effecten ervan worden steeds zichtbaarder. Dit geldt met name voor twee gebieden: de productie van binnenlandse machines voor de vervaardiging en assemblage van droneonderdelen, zelfs wanneer die machines nog steeds afhankelijk zijn van buitenlandse elektronica, en de ontwikkeling van communicatie- en besturingsmethoden waarmee drones op middellange en lange afstanden kunnen opereren zonder afhankelijk te zijn van Starlink.

De technologische voorsprong die Oekraïne in het voorjaar en de zomer van 2026 genoot, wordt snel kleiner. Als Oekraïne er niet in slaagt die voorsprong te behouden, zou Rusland het komende jaar zowel wat betreft productieschaal als technologisch een voorsprong kunnen nemen.

Dit betekent niet noodzakelijkerwijs dat de algemene dynamiek van de oorlog zal veranderen, maar het is duidelijk een van de kwesties die de Oekraïense militaire leiding in de nabije toekomst zal moeten aanpakken.

Dmytro Putiata @kriegsfor… · 2 u

Het Russische leger lanceert elke 24 uur 1.500 tot 2.000 drones tegen Druzjkivka en twee logistieke routes die naar de stad leiden. En dat zijn alleen radiografisch bestuurde FPV-drones, dus zonder de aanvallen met FPV-drones via glasvezelkabel (onmogelijk te tellen). Het Oekraïense 19e Legerkorps staat zwaar onder druk.

Als we het hebben over de richting Dobropillja, lanceert het Russische leger ongeveer 1.200 radiografisch bestuurde FPV-drones per 24 uur.

Het aantal drones en drone operators neemt voortdurend toe.

text:
Similar situation now except: North Vietnam = Iran, Spirit of Glassboro = Spirit of Anchorage.

History After Dark  

On June 23, 1967, Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin quietly delivered a secret peace offer to Lyndon Johnson. Meeting in the quiet college town of Glassboro, New Jersey, the leaders of the Cold War’s rival superpowers had escaped their aides to eat lunch inside a borrowed Victorian house. Between courses, Kosygin leaned forward to share information he insisted was in strict confidence: Moscow had contacted Hanoi, and North Vietnam was prepared to begin direct peace talks if the United States halted its bombing campaign. For an American president whose domestic agenda was being swallowed by an escalating jungle war, the Soviet premier was dangling an unexpected exit from a national nightmare.
The setting for this extraordinary diplomatic encounter was entirely accidental. Two weeks earlier, the Six-Day War in the Middle East had pushed Washington and Moscow to activate their emergency teletype hotline, prompting Kosygin to travel to New York to address the United Nations. Johnson sought a face-to-face summit, but protocol created an immediate impasse: Kosygin refused to visit the White House to avoid appearing subservient to his communist allies, while Johnson refused to travel to New York and pay court to a foreign visitor. The compromise was Glassboro State College, a small campus located exactly halfway between both capitals. Inside Hollybush, the home of the college president, the two men met upstairs in a private dining room, joined only by Soviet interpreter Viktor Sukhodrev. Outside, thousands of local residents crowded the sunny lawn with handwritten welcome signs, unaware that the fate of the war was being debated over lunch.
The private meeting brought together two men trapped by opposing political pressures. Johnson, a towering Texan of immense domestic ambition, was watching his Great Society crumble under the weight of mounting casualties, spiraling budgets, and anti-war demonstrations that chanted outside his bedroom window. Kosygin, a solemn, austere technocrat who governed alongside Soviet Party leader Leonid Brezhnev, had his own treacherous balance to maintain. Beijing was already accusing the Kremlin of betraying world revolution by fraternizing with American imperialists. Yet Kosygin genuinely feared that the conflict in Southeast Asia would trigger an accidental global catastrophe. By acting as an intermediary for Hanoi, the Soviet premier hoped to extinguish the Cold War’s most dangerous flashpoint while keeping Moscow’s leadership intact.
Yet as Kosygin urged Johnson to halt Operation Rolling Thunder, the American president confronted an agonizing military dilemma. Top military advisers, including General William Westmoreland and the Joint Chiefs of Staff, insisted that any pause in the bombing would allow North Vietnamese divisions to pour fresh troops and heavy artillery across the Demilitarized Zone to slaughter American forces. Looking directly at Kosygin across the table, Johnson posed a blunt question: if the premier were in his position, would he stop firing while the other side kept shooting? Kosygin pushed back with equal firmness, arguing that Hanoi was a proud, sovereign nation that would never negotiate under the barrel of an American gun. The premier urged Johnson to demonstrate the courage of a superpower by taking the first step, assuring him that formal negotiations would begin almost immediately.
The diplomatic opening ultimately shattered against deep mutual suspicion. Johnson refused to stop the bombing without an ironclad guarantee of military reciprocity, demanding that Hanoi cease infiltrating troops into South Vietnam. But Kosygin could make no such commitment; fiercely protective of its independence, the North Vietnamese leadership accepted Soviet weapons but flatly refused to take operational orders from Moscow. When Johnson later formalized his conditions in the San Antonio formula—offering a bombing halt only if Hanoi promised not to exploit the pause—North Vietnam denounced the proposal as imperialist extortion. The press hailed the warm personal rapport between the two leaders as the "Spirit of Glassboro," but behind the smiles, the secret peace channel had completely closed.
The tragic consequence of that deadlock materialized seven months later. In January 1968, communist forces launched the massive Tet Offensive across South Vietnam, shattering the White House’s claims of steady military progress and breaking the American public’s faith in the war. The political fallout destroyed Johnson’s presidency. In March 1968, an exhausted, aging Johnson appeared on national television to announce a partial bombing halt and declare that he would not seek reelection. The very concession Kosygin had urged Johnson to make in the quiet dining room at Hollybush was finally granted from a position of political defeat, but by then, thousands more American and Vietnamese lives had been lost, and the war would grind on for five more bloody years.

Gold Movie

Gold is a 2016 American epic crime drama film directed by Stephen Gaghan and written by Patrick Massett and John Zinman. The film stars Matthew McConaughey, Édgar Ramírez, Bryce Dallas Howard, Corey Stoll, Toby Kebbell, Craig T. Nelson, Stacy Keach and Bruce Greenwood. The film is loosely based on the true story of the 1997 Bre-X mining scandal, when a massive gold deposit was supposedly discovered in the jungles of Indonesia; however, for legal reasons and to enhance the appeal of the film, character names and story details were changed.

News Flashback

Early 2026

Jan-March

Streaming Wars

The "Streaming Wars" refers to the intense competition among digital media platforms to dominate the subscription video-on-demand (SVOD) market by capturing and retaining global audiences.

As of early 2026, the landscape has shifted from a period of rapid expansion into a phase of major consolidation and a focus on profitability over subscriber volume.

The "Winner" and Current State (2026)

Netflix Dominance: Industry analysts increasingly cite Netflix as the victor. In January 2026, Netflix reported 18% year-over-year revenue growth and is currently pursuing a high-stakes $83 billion all-cash acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery’s studio and streaming assets (including HBO/Max).

The "Big 3": Despite fierce competition, the market is primarily dominated by Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+.

YouTube's Rise: Some experts argue YouTube is the true winner of the broader attention economy, surpassing traditional streaming services in total viewership by pivoting back to user-generated content.
Key Strategies in 2026

Consolidation: Smaller or struggling services are being shuttered or merged. For example, Disney recently shut down Hulu as a standalone service.

Monetization Shifts: Platforms have moved away from "growth at all costs" to strategies like password-sharing crackdowns, ad-supported tiers, and price hikes.

Live Sports & Events: Services are increasingly bidding on live sports rights (e.g., Netflix hosting WWE's Raw starting in 2025) to differentiate their offerings.

Bundling: To combat "subscription fatigue," platforms are forming strategic partnerships with telecommunications companies and banks to offer bundled service hubs.

Consumer Impact

Price Hikes: Many consumers are canceling services due to rising costs; over 40% of Americans cited price as their primary reason for unsubscribing in late 2025.

Resurgence of Piracy: Fragmented content and high costs have led to a significant comeback for pirate sites, which some users now find more comprehensive than paid services.

"South Park: The Streaming Wars": The term was popularized in mainstream culture by a 2-part South Park special released on Paramount+ in 2022, which satirized the industry's aggressive competition.

Gold (1974)

Gold is a 1974 British action-thriller directed by Peter R. Hunt, starring Roger Moore and Susannah York. Based on the 1970 novel Gold Mine by Wilbur Smith, the film is set in the South African goldfields and follows a conspiracy by a global syndicate to manipulate the price of gold by sabotaging a rich mine.

Plot: Rod Slater (Moore), a newly appointed general manager, is manipulated by his boss, Manfred Steyner (Bradford Dillman), into drilling through a protective barrier into a subterranean lake. This is intended to flood the mine, causing a global gold shortage and driving up prices for a greedy cabal.

Production Controversy: The film was controversially shot on location in South Africa during the apartheid era. This led to a "black ban" by British film unions, though some crew members defied it to work on the production.

James Bond Connection: Many crew members were veterans of the James Bond franchise, including director Peter Hunt (On Her Majesty's Secret Service), editor John Glen, and title designer Maurice Binder.

Accolades: The film received an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song for "Wherever Love Takes Me," composed by Elmer Bernstein and sung by Maureen McGovern.

text:
It went much further than a rumor — Netflix actually signed a definitive deal to acquire Warner Bros., but the deal was ultimately killed by a higher Paramount Skydance bid.

The timeline is:

December 5, 2025: Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery announced a definitive transaction. Netflix would acquire Warner Bros. film & TV studios, HBO and HBO Max, after WBD separated its linear-network assets into Discovery Global. The deal valued the Warner assets at about $82.7 billion enterprise value / $72 billion equity value. 
January 20, 2026: Netflix and WBD strengthened the agreement by converting it to an all-cash $27.75-per-share offer. 
February 2026: Paramount Skydance came back with a substantially richer proposal: $31 per WBD share in cash, plus stronger regulatory protections and payment of the breakup fee owed to Netflix. 
February 26: Netflix decided not to increase its bid, saying that at the price necessary to beat Paramount the acquisition was no longer financially attractive. 
February 27: WBD formally terminated the Netflix merger agreement and signed with Paramount Skydance instead. Paramount paid Netflix the contractual $2.8 billion termination fee. 

So today the situation is essentially:

Netflix + Warner Bros. ❌ cancelled
Paramount Skydance + Warner Bros. Discovery ⏳ still pending

The Paramount/WBD transaction is enormous—roughly $110 billion enterprise value—and unlike Netflix’s proposal it involves acquiring essentially all of Warner Bros. Discovery, rather than just Warner/HBO after spinning off the cable networks. 

There is an important wrinkle as of September 15, 2026: the Paramount-Warner transaction still hasn’t closed. It has received numerous regulatory clearances, including the EU in July and UK in August, but it faces lawsuits from California and other states plus the Writers Guild of America seeking to stop the merger on antitrust grounds. Paramount has voluntarily delayed completion while that litigation proceeds; a trial is currently scheduled for March 2027, although settlement discussions are continuing. 

So the interesting counterfactual is that we came surprisingly close to getting a company combining Netflix + HBO + Warner Bros. + DC + Harry Potter + Game of Thrones + the Warner film library. Instead, Netflix walked away with a $2.8 billion breakup payment, while Paramount is now trying to create an even broader Paramount + CBS + Warner Bros. + HBO + CNN + DC media group.

If you want, I can also show you what the Netflix-Warner empire would have looked like vs the proposed Paramount-Warner empire, including all studios, streaming services, TV networks and major franchises.

🚨 Nearly 1,000 e-bikes, e-motorcycles, e-scooters and pocket bikes were surrendered Sunday at Orange County’s first buyback at Angel Stadium in Anaheim. Officials said the vehicles filled nine 26-foot U-Haul trucks.

The OC District Attorney’s Office offered $200–$1,000 gift cards from Target, Walmart and Dick’s Sporting Goods. text:
#rentomojo

Business Model &  unit economics of Rentomojo explained: 

RentoMojo operates a vertically integrated, full-stack subscription platform for home furniture and appliances. It is a major player in India’s shifting rental economy, catering heavily to transient urban professionals.

1. Revenue Model: highly predictable, recurring, and structured around the product lifecycle

Subscription Rentals (~98% of Revenue): The core engine. Customers pay a monthly recurring fee to rent furniture (50.6% mix) and appliances (47.2% mix).

Re-Commerce & E-Commerce: The company runs secondary channels to sell off older inventory or allow consumers an outright option to purchase their rented items

2. Cost Structure: RentoMojo functions via a capital-intensive, asset-heavy framework that relies heavily on continuous reinvestment:

Asset Procurement (CapEx): The heaviest drain on capital. A massive portion of operational cash is funneled directly back into buying new inventory.

Warehousing & Reverse Logistics: Managing localized distribution centers and the continuous pick-up/drop-off ecosystem.

+ Refurbishment & Maintenance Operations
+ Financing Costs: Servicing debt used to scale up the core asset base.

3. Margin Profile
EBITDA Margins: Exceptionally healthy at 41.5% to 42.2% (FY26), driven by strong recurring income and high asset utilization (~83.3%).

PAT Margins: Reported at 27% for FY26 (Net Profit of ₹104.3 Crore on Total Income of ₹394 Crore). If one time deferred tax payment in FY26 is deducated, then it is about 16% 

4. Market Dynamics

The organized rental market slice is rapidly expanding, climbing from ₹350 Crore in 2021 to ₹1,550 Crore in 2025, with expectations to cross ₹6,030 Crore by 2030. With an estimated 4.8 crore rental apartments across India, penetration remains in its infancy.

Demand & Supply Characteristics

DEMAND SIDE
• Gen-Z & Millennial urban mobility
• Asset-light lifestyle preferences
• Avoidance of heavy upfront capital costs

SUPPLY SIDE
• Large-scale asset inventory (8.5L+ active items)
• Centralized refurbishing centers
• In-house reverse logistics network

5. Economic Moat Profile

Pricing Power (Moderate), Switching Costs (High over time), Barriers to entry (High - The capital intensity needed to establish warehouses, purchase massive scale inventory, and seamlessly execute reverse logistics prevents agile, pure-software competitors from easily entering the market)

6. Valuation & Growth Prospects

P/E - Priced at roughly 40x FY26 earnings
Risk: heavily structured as an Offer for Sale (OFS)

Future Growth Prospects

Geographical Scaling: Replicating its success beyond the top 10 core metros (which currently generate ~89.5% of revenue) into Tier-2 hubs like Indore and Lucknow.

Cohort Maturation (Leverage): RentoMojo's historical data indicates that mature product cohorts routinely yield over 4x returns on their initial procurement cost, implying that as their inventory ages gracefully, cash flow metrics should dramatically improve.

Drivers of growth:

The "Locked-In" Revenue Pipeline - Entered FY27 with ₹292.57 Crore already guaranteed via active, unexpired rental contracts.

Structural Industry Tailwinds in organized rental market for home furniture and home appliances 

Private Labels: manufacturing partnership with Dixon Technologies to produce private-label appliances reduces upfront procurement costs ==> higher yields

Unit Economics: 

1: Asset Yield & Lifecycle Efficiency
- how efficiently RentoMojo treats its inventory as a cash-generating engine

Asset Turn / Gross Rental Yield (Exceptional):
RentoMojo’s asset cohorts display excellent long-term compounding. Data(RHP) shows that their FY17 asset cohort has earned 5.1 times its original cost over a decade, while their FY18 cohort has earned 4.5 times cost. This implies an average annualized gross rental yield of 45% to 50% relative to the initial CapEx spent on the item

Payback Period per Asset (Healthy): The initial cash outflow to procure an appliance or furniture piece is fully recovered within 18 to 22 months of active deployment, after which the asset generates pure contribution profit (minus refurbishing fees).

Asset Utilization / Occupancy Rate (Strong but Moderating): As RentoMojo scaled its live items from 4.6 Lakh in FY24 to 8.51 Lakh items in FY26, its occupancy rate shifted slightly from 86.4% down to 83.3%. A utilization rate sustained above 83% ensures that asset depreciation is overwhelmingly covered by incoming rental invoices rather than sitting dead in warehouses.

Refurbishment Multiply Effect (High Efficiency): RentoMojo processes returned items with massive financial leverage. In FY26, the company executed over 6 Lakh asset refurbishments at a total operational cost of ₹19 Crore. Against a total revenue of ₹387 Crore, deep cleaning and repairing returned items costs the business less than 5% of its total revenue, allowing items to safely undergo 3 to 5 distinct multi-year customer cycles over a 10-year lifespan.

2: Subscriber Monetisation & Cohort Quality
This category gauges how much it costs to acquire a user versus the predictable value they return.

Average Tenure / Contract Sticky Rate (High Visibility): The average subscription tenure for a RentoMojo customer stands at 18.04 months. Because user agreements lock in tenures up front, RentoMojo entered FY27 with ₹292.5 Crore in unbilled, contractually secured forward revenue. This makes revenue highly predictable and independent of constant marketing acquisition cycles.

Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC) Payback (Fair): Performance marketing spend grew by 86.3% to ₹20.9 Crore in FY26 (up from ₹11.2 Crore in FY25) as the company aggressively acquired a live base of 2.53 Lakh active subscribers. While absolute customer acquisition costs are rising due to competitive pressure from players like Furlenco, the front-loaded marketing CAC is successfully amortized within the first 4 to 5 months of a subscriber’s 18-month tenure.

LTV to CAC Ratio (Strong): Given an 18-month average tenure and high gross rental yields, a single user profile yields a Net Lifetime Value that sits comfortably at 3.5x to 4x their acquisition cost, well clearing the institutional venture and public market benchmark of 3x

3: Leakage & Friction Metrics
- highlights the functional risks that put pressure on RentoMojo's cash flows.

Reverse Logistics & Handling Cost (Increasing):
major operational friction point as physical store and warehouse footprints expand.

Collection Leakage & Default Risk (Critical Monitorable):  rapid inflation of Trade Receivables, which scaled up to 21% of revenue (Uncollected monthly rental invoice, defaults)

Valuation summary: 

EV/EBIDTA of 27x (at IPO price) reflects a premium price tag - valuing its highly predictable, subscription model much like a fast growing tech company, rather than legacy asset leasing business.
