text:
IMMIGRATION
A serious discussion on immigration
The problem
Legal asylum seekers are not really the problem. In fact, if someone arrives to the UK legally, has the correct documentation to enter the country and seeks asylum, then that’s fine. The problem with legal asylum seekers is that documentation can take anywhere from six months to over a year to process.
So, what happens to these asylum seekers once they have submitted the documentation?
Applicants generally receive a temporary identification card or document (such as an Application Registration Card in the UK) confirming their identity and legal presence while they await a decision. The problem with this is that they ‘disappear’. They Don’t have the right to work in Britain whilst they are waiting a decision, unless the claim has taken over 12 months. Then they can claim for a limited work permit. Until they have that, they are given Government support and benefits. However, many lose patience with waiting for documentation, whilst others have their application turned down. These people ‘disappear’. The home office figures for people that they have no track of, puts the number of people at 50,000+. And don’t forget, these are the Legal ones, those that entered Great Britain legally!
The Illegal Immigration Problem
And then we must consider the illegal side of immigration.
The fundamentals are that immigrants leave their natural homes in Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Syria, Somalia and many other places, in some cases where there ARE wars taking place for their own safety. And they travel to Europe. Now the rules of the EU state that immigrants seeking asylum, should settle “…in the first safe haven…”. However, there is absolutely reams of documentation to state that these people, far from settling in the first safe haven, travel thousands of miles across Europe and settle in France, at least on a temporary basis. Their target is Great Britain. They are then subjected to the organising gangs that promise them a new life in Britain, and that they can organise passage on a small boat. The small boat turns out to be a dinghy or a rib, and more recently a so called mega dinghy…an oversized, commercial-grade inflatable rubber boat, capable of carry up to 300 people at a time. However, these things are not built to cross the English channel, one of the busiest and most dangerous waterways in the world!
So why do they come to Great Britain?
People arriving in the UK without authorization are generally barred from mainstream welfare benefits and social housing under "no recourse to public funds" rules. However, almost everyone arriving this way immediately claims asylum. If they register as an asylum seeker and prove they are destitute, they often discard their passports before travelling, they can receive basic government:
Accommodation: A place to live, such as a      dispersal house, flat, or contingency hotel, assigned by the Home Office.
Financial      Support:     Around £49.18 per person per week loaded onto an ASPEN debit card for food      and essentials (or less if meals are provided in accommodation).
Healthcare: Free access to emergency      and primary NHS care.

Because there have been so many of them, they were initially housed in old army camps, however, they complained that the facilities were too basic, so the Government began to house them in hotels. But this met with widespread criticism from British people, and although some are still used, the Government have moved many into HMO (houses of multiple occupation). Not only that, but there are reports that many of these illegal immigrants, receive a lot of free benefits such as mobile phones, cinema tickets amongst other free stuff.

The Government, under pressure to stop these illegal immigrants have paid France £662 million, in an agreement where French authorities would stop the immigrants trying to cross the channel. However, the agreement has face fierce criticism as the French authorities have been seen standing by whilst immigrants board and set sail! In one or two instances, the French Navy have actually provided an escort for small boats to cross the channel!  The initial Government response, under Sir Keir Starmer, was that the Government would actively go after the gangs that organise the crossings. As of May 2026, around 300 so called ‘people smugglers’, have been arrested and charged. However, whilst this sounds impressive, there are no exact totals for the number of individual people smugglers, as they operate within shifting, clandestine international networks rather than transparent registries. If one leader is arrested, he or she is almost immediately replaced with another to carry on.

It is worth mentioning that many of these illegal immigrants are not put through the process of a security or background check. The authorities have no idea if these people have criminal records in their own country. Therefore, it is logical to assume that some of them might have, and if they do, what crimes have they committed? It could be that they have committed a murder, an assault or a crime that in this country would see them placed on a sexual register. It is certainly a fact that a percentage of them have a very different view of how women and children should be treated and there are documented cases of immigrants, illegal or otherwise, being convicted of sexual harassment, assault and rape.
There is no logical argument that can be put forward to suggest that admitting thousands of unchecked people from diversly different backgrounds, many of whom cannot speak English and have no intention of integrating into our society or even adhering to our laws, should be freely admitted to this country.

I just want to diversify for a second. I’d just like to offer some basic insight, that everyone seems to have ignored.
These people, pay out an average of £5,000 to climb onto a dinghy or ‘super’ dinghy, that will take them across the English Channel, to enter Great Britain illegally. They are breaking English law, quite openly, therefore they are committing an illegal act, thus they are criminals, and should be treated as criminals first and foremost, before they are given any sort of help or support.

Of course, for every argument against these ILLEGAL immigrants, there is a counter argument, mainly proposed by Government supporters and leftwing activists.

“It is unfair to say that all of these immigrants are rapist and will carry out acts of sexual harassment and worse”

It would be entirely wrong to suggest that Great Britain does not have natives that don’t commit such crimes. However, I think most people would accept that these crimes should be dealt with by the police forces and criminal justice departments that we already have in this country. Dealing with foreigners convicted of one or more of the same crimes is much more complicated, involving extra costs such as interpreters and liaison officers depending on which country they are from.

“Everyone should be welcome”, they say.
Yes, everyone who arrives to these shores WITH authorisation is welcome to apply for asylum or the right to remain. NOT those that arrive illegally.

“They are fleeing oppression in their own countries”, is another argument that is put forward.
If that is the case, then why don’t they simply travel (or escape) to the first safe country? Oh no, apparently that isn’t good enough. Even remaining in France isn’t apparently good enough, they have to come to Britain, and it is difficult to argue that they come here simply because of our soft benefits system.
“A lot of them are vulnerable women and children”, is an often-heard cry, which is actually rubbish. Of course, there are a percentage of women and children, but they are far outweighed by the number of men, many of them below the age of forty!

It always seems strange to me that the leftists claim that these immigrants SHOULD be given places to stay, and yet when asked, they wouldn’t offer them a room or a place to stay in their Homes!!

SOLUTIONS

It is all very well to stand in Parliament and say that the immigration problem will be solved under your government. Both the Conservatives and Labour have promised to tackle the problem. But none of their solutions or methods have worked. 
It is quite clear that illegal immigration is a problem and that despite paying the French millions of £’s, they are not that committed to solving the problem at source. Indeed, the thinking seems to be that by allowing these immigrants to sail away, they are reliving France of a social and economic problem. In other words, move the problem on so they don’t have to worry about it.
Reform UK have suggested that employing the British Royal Navy to intercept and return illegal immigrants in mid channel to France. The problem with that is, that the Royal Navy only has six Coastal Patrol Vessels (CPVs)! It is presumed that these are for use not only in the English Channel, but elsewhere as well. Therefore, more would be needed in order to implement these Channel patrols, which of course would cost a lot of money to build.
As we have stated, those arriving by (relatively) small boats, are breaking English laws and should be treated as criminals. Therefore, they should be arrested, jailed and prosecuted first and foremost with that crime, and if convicted and handed a prison sentence, serve their sentence and then immediately deported, because after all, Great Britain doesn’t want foreign criminals living freely in our society.
The next solution is a moral one. If Britain was seen to be a lot harder on illegal immigration by reducing benefits to a bar minimum, then a lot of the incentives for coming to this country would be removed.
House them in purpose-built detention centres, feed them, clothe them if necessary, then process them before either granting them asylum or returning them to whence they came. And do all this within two months. This may sound harsh, but it is a big problem and harsh measures are needed.
There is a very odd rule that is in force. It says that: You cannot apply for asylum from outside the UK or through a British embassy abroad. There is no specific "asylum visa" available for travel. 
And yet, British embassies and consulates abroad are considered British Sovereign territory. So, why cannot those applying for asylum in Great Britain do so in their local embassy or consulate. It is understood that this cannot always be done in a war torn country, however, it COULD be done if the applicant made it to the first safe country and applied from there.
The problem is, that if immigrants have to have their feet on British soil to apply, then the moment that illegal immigrants (those without authorisation), set foot on British soil, they are breaking the law. Refer to the previous argument above.
Without doubt, immigration, illegal or otherwise is a huge problem for Great Britain, and other parts of the world. So far, our British governments have not dealt with it very well, preferring a soft option, that allows thousands of them to arrive, and then trying to deal with any problems afterwards.
The arguments on both sides are emotive and people get very passionate about them. However, a solution has to be arrived at very soon, because the normally placid people of Great Britain are losing their patience with governments that promise much and deliver very little.

🚨🇨🇳 TAIWAN'S SEPARATISTS IN SHOCK: CHINA’S NEW MODULE TURNS DRONES INTO MULTI-ROUND CARRIERS

Chinese drone manufacturer Huanyu has demonstrated a modular release system that allows multicopters to carry several cylindrical payloads and drop them separately or in a single salvo.

Recent footage shows several multi-cell units, while a smaller two-cell module is mounted on a drone and releases one object in flight.

🔸 The key development is not a new airframe, but a modular and scalable payload package. Different racks can be matched to the host drone’s size and lifting capacity, allowing operators to trade endurance and maneuverability for a larger load without redesigning the aircraft.

🔸 Huanyu’s strike-equipment catalog includes 60 mm, 80 mm and 120 mm throwers, an electrically fired 38 mm smoke launcher and an 82 mm multi-round dispenser.

🔸 The 82 mm family is offered in 2-, 4-, 6-, 8- and 10-cell versions. According to the manufacturer, payloads can be released individually or all at once. The modules use clamp mounting, onboard power and SBUS/PWM control signals.

🔸 With armed payloads, individual-or-salvo release would allow one drone to deliver munitions at several points during a sortie or drop its entire load in a single pass. That increases the number of rounds carried by each airframe and controlled by each operator.

🔸 Huanyu markets related systems for military reconnaissance and strike missions. However, the latest footage does not identify the released objects, show an explosion or confirm adoption by the People’s Liberation Army. It demonstrates a scalable carrier and release system, not a fielded Chinese strike-drone fleet.

If adopted by the PLA, modules like these could turn compatible low-cost multicopters into multi-round strike platforms for a Taiwan contingency.

Instead of building a purpose-designed combat drone around every weapon, China could pair different payload racks with compatible airframes and increase the number of munitions delivered on each sortie.

The threat would come not from one sophisticated drone, but from large numbers of adaptable carriers able to deliver several rounds before air defenses can stop them.

Do you think modular payloads are more useful than purpose-built attack drones?

text:
I need to say something that has been sitting with me for a long time.

I know exactly what X is. I know about the bubbles, the squads, the multiple accounts used to create a fake sense of numbers. I know how this platform works. And honestly, that is not even what disappoints me the most.

What disappoints me is seeing people who claim to love Taehyung acting like they are completely incapable of doing anything for him themselves.

And before anyone gets offended: I am NOT talking about everyone. If this doesn't describe you, then don't take it personally. I'm talking about the people who know exactly what I mean.

It is 2026.

TEN YEARS.

For ten years, Taehyung has had to move forward without the kind of consistent support he should have received from the wider BTS fandom, the company and BTS fanbases in so many situations.

And we STILL have people begging or demanding that BTS fanbases post updates about him?

Honestly? It's embarrassing.

We should have understood by now that Taehyung fans don't need to sit around waiting for someone else to give us space.

Want to help Taehyung? THEN DO IT.

Stream. Vote. Promote his work. Support his projects. Focus on his releases, his brand deals, his achievements and his career. Create projects for HIM. Put your energy into HIM.

But instead, some people spend their entire day feeding shipping theories.

Now it's a shoe. Tomorrow it's a photo. Then it's some random coincidence. They take one tiny detail and build an entire story around it, as if it proves something.

IT DOESN'T.

Whether Taehyung traveled with anyone or not is NOT confirmed just because someone spotted a similar shoe, outfit, location or whatever else

Stop turning random details into "proof" to feed a shipping narrative.

And then his name gets dragged into another war.

DEFENDING WHO?

Taehyung is a global artist. He has friends, connections, respect and a life outside your fandom bubble. He works, lives, travels, has fun and builds relationships.

LET THE MAN LIVE.

Everything has to be connected to someone. Everything becomes a theory. Everything becomes a comparison. Everything becomes a war.

If he's with someone, there's a problem. If he's alone, there's a problem. If he has a friendship, there's a problem. If he travels, people invent stories. If he happens to wear something similar to someone else, suddenly there's a whole investigation.

You don't even allow Taehyung to have a life without turning it into fandom drama.

And the worst part?

You do it "for him."

STOP.

You do not own Taehyung's life. You do not speak for him. You don't get to decide who he can be friends with, talk to, travel with or spend time with.

And honestly, some of this behavior is starting to look like ARMY 2.0.

You claim to hate that behavior while repeating the same cycle: wars, comparisons, demands, obsession with other fandoms and constantly putting Taehyung in the middle of everything.

That is not support.

That is not protection.

That is not love.

It is a DISSERVICE.

And somehow, some people can't organize one meaningful project focused on Taehyung, but they always have time to follow shipping theories, attack others and drag his name into every possible fight.

So before you post another tweet, stop for five seconds and ask yourself:

"Does this actually help Taehyung, or am I just feeding another unconfirmed narrative?"

Because if this is all you have to offer, then honestly, step aside.

Let the people who actually want to work for Taehyung work.

And learn what being a fan actually means.

A fan supports. A fan promotes. A fan votes. A fan streams. A fan celebrates. A fan respects.

A fan does NOT control the artist's life.

Think before you post.

Because you're exhausting the very people who are here to support Taehyung

$BTC 📈

75.5K VAH remains THE key HTF level to monitor! 🔍

As long as price holds above value, this remains a straight forward consolidation following the impulsive move higher - essentially processing the expansion before another attempt to break the HTF bearish market structure around 82K.

The picture changes if we lose VAH and accept back inside value. Below ~75.5K, there is relatively little structural support from the recent move, which leaves room for price to rebalance the inefficiencies created during the fast expansion higher.

My first downside reference is the low AVWAP around 70K. Below that, attention shifts toward the previous internal range highs / Golden Pocket, POC and the deeper range references.

For the bullish case, the setup I want to see is very specific: Sweep the local lows → test VAH/liquidity → absorption in OrderFlow → reclaim and hold above VAH. That would offer a potential long setup back toward the local highs / 82K area, with continuation higher possible if the HTF structure finally breaks.

So this is an important test for the bulls! 🍿

The reaction around 75.5K should tell us whether the market is genuinely accepting above the old range/value, or whether the recent move was simply an excursion above value before rotating back through it as we are not ready yet to start a new bullish market regime.

text:
🔥The Sacred Sacrifice on Nallur's Streets...

Thileepan's Non-Violent Resistance and the Moral Fortitude of an Oppressed Nation

The profound poetic testament, "The child who transcended the absolute boundaries of sacrifice, there are no words to fully sing of Thileepan; sing of the name of the one who became a holy offering in sacrifice for thousands of ages," is not a mere emotional lamentation. It marks the ultimate spiritual and ideological apex of the Eelam Tamil national liberation movement. On the dawn of September 16, 1987, on the sacred streets surrounding the Nallur Kandaswamy Temple in Jaffna, a twenty-two-year-old political cadre, Thileepan (Rasiah Partheepan), initiated a fast unto death, refusing even a single drop of water, to demand five fundamental political prerequisites from the Indian state. This legendary fast remains the most radical configuration of non-violent resistance (Ahimsa) in modern global history. Dissolving his physical existence over twelve agonizing days against the geopolitical hegemony of New Delhi and the majoritarian unitary apparatus of Colombo, Thileepan transformed the streets of Nallur into a permanent altar of moral resistance.

Theoretically and conceptually, Thileepan’s fast was not a passive act of despair; it was the ultimate weaponization of moral fortitude by an oppressed nationality. In a brilliant strategic turn of history, the very doctrine of non-violent resistance championed by Mahatma Gandhi was deployed against the central Indian state, which had entered the island via the Indo-Lanka Accord to neutralize the sovereign aspirations of the Tamils. To the global discourse that routinely attempts to categorize indigenous resistance as "terrorism," Thileepan offered his own physical body as an unyielding text of peaceful protest. By systematically executing this ultimate fast for the distinct five-point demands, his sacrifice effectively secured the absolute moral superiority of the Eelam Tamil nation before the principles of international humanitarian law.

Within contemporary diaspora discourses, where surface-level liberal pacifism often dominates and gaslights history by claiming "war is bad on both sides," Thileepan’s legacy serves as a vital ideological correction. The streets of Nallur endure as a historical witness to how passionately the Tamil nation pursued peace, and the monumental price its individual cadres were willing to pay to protect homeland sovereignty. In an era where the current administration led by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake and southern leftist formations attempt to minimize the Tamil national question to minor economic doles, Thileepan’s historic demands remain inextricably linked to the non-negotiable right to self-determination. While institutional Tamil political parties, including ITAK, remain fractured by short-sighted parliamentary careerism, the sacred memory of Thileepan functions as the ultimate moral catalyst uniting the global Tamil collective.

Ultimately, viewed through the lens of comprehensive Tamil Nationalist political theory, the name of Thileepan is not a relic of historical trauma; it is an enduring strategic compass for sovereign survival. Though words fall short of encapsulating his monumental transition into martyrdom, the ideological decree he authored through his ultimate fast emphasizes that the collective rights of the Eelam Tamils can never be compromised. Refusing to become passive pawns in majoritarian state-centric rivalries or shifting international alignments, the Tamil nation must preserve its strategic unity. Anchoring its global diplomatic struggle to the sacred memory of its martyrs and the unyielding political consciousness of its indigenous population remains the definitive historical imperative to honor the eternal light of Thieepan.

- Krishna Ambalavanar

"தியாகத்தின் எல்லையை மீறிய பிள்ளை, திலீபனை பாடிட வார்த்தைகள் இல்லை; தியாகத்தில் ஆகுதி ஆனவன் நாமத்தை, ஆயிரம் ஆயிரம் காலங்கள் பாடுங்கள்" 

என்ற வரிகள், 
உணர்ச்சிகளின் வெளிப்பாடு மட்டுமல்ல; அவை ஈழத்தமிழ்த்தேசிய வரலாற்றின் ஆக உன்னதமான ஒரு சித்தாந்தப் பெருநெருப்பை நமக்கு நினைவூட்டுகின்றன. 

1987 செப்டம்பர் 16 அதிகாலை யாழ்ப்பாணம் நல்லூர் கந்தசுவாமி ஆலயத்தின் வீதியில், இருபத்தி இரண்டு வயதே நிரம்பிய இளம் போராளி திலீபன் (இராசையா பார்த்தீபன்) ஐந்து அம்சக் கோரிக்கைகளை முன்வைத்து, நீர் கூட அருந்தாமல் தொடங்கிய உண்ணாநோன்புப் போராட்டம் என்பது உலக வரலாற்றில் அஹிம்சையின் உச்சகட்ட எல்லையாகும். 

இந்தியப் பேரரசின் பிராந்திய மேலாதிக்க வாதத்திற்கும், கொழும்பு அதிகார மையங்களின் பேரினவாதக் கட்டமைப்புக்கும் எதிராக, ஒரு சொட்டு நீர் கூட அருந்தாமல் பன்னிரண்டு நாட்கள் தன் உடலையே உருக்கி, அந்த நல்லூர் வீதியைத் தியாக யாகத்தின் பலிபீடமாக மாற்றிய திலீபனின் அரசியல் நகர்வு, சமகாலப் புவிசார் அரசியல் சூழலில் மீண்டும் ஆழமாகத் தத்துவார்த்த ரீதியாக பகுப்பாய்வு செய்யப்பட வேண்டிய ஒன்றாகும்.

அரசியல் கோட்பாடுகளின் அடிப்படையில் பார்க்கும்போது, திலீபனின் உண்ணாநோன்பு என்பது வெறும் உணர்ச்சிவசப்பட்ட மரணக் கோரிக்கை அல்ல; அது ஒடுக்கப்பட்ட ஒரு தேசிய இனத்தின் தார்மீக அறச் சீற்றத்தின்  உச்சக்கட்ட வடிவமாகும். 

மகாத்மா காந்தி இந்தியாவுக்குக் கற்றுக்கொடுத்த அஹிம்சைப் போராட்ட வடிவத்தை, அதே இந்தியப் பேரரசு இலங்கை-இந்திய ஒப்பந்தத்தின் மூலம் ஈழ மண்ணில் தமிழ் மக்களின் தன்னுரிமையை நசுக்க முற்பட்ட போது, அதே இந்திய அரசுக்கு எதிராக அஹிம்சையைக் கேடயமாகப் பயன்படுத்திய வரலாற்றுச் சாதுரியம் திலீபனுடையது.

 "பயங்கரவாதிகள்" என்று தமிழ் மக்களின் தற்காப்புப் போராட்டத்தை உலகிற்குச் சித்தரிக்க முயன்ற பேரினவாத அரசுகளுக்கு முன்னால், தங்களின் நியாயமான ஐந்து அம்சக் கோரிக்கைகளுக்காகத் தன் சொந்த உடலையே ஆயுதமாக மாற்றி, தியாகத்தில் ஆகுதியான திலீபனின் உன்னதம், ஈழத்தமிழர் தேசத்தின் தார்மீக மேன்மையை சர்வதேசச் சட்ட விதிகளுக்கு முன்னால் நிரூபித்துக் காட்டியது. 

சமகாலப் புலம்பெயர் சூழலில், *மேற்கத்திய லிபரல் (சமூகத் தாராளவாதம்) அமைதிவாதப் பொறிகளுக்குள் சிக்கி "யுத்தம் இருதரப்பிற்குமே நல்லதல்ல" என்று ஒடுக்குபவனையும் ஒடுக்கப்படுபவனையும் சமப்படுத்தும் வரலாற்று அறியாமை கொண்ட இளையோருக்கு மத்தியில், திலீபனின் வரலாறு ஒரு பெரும் சித்தாந்தப் பாடமாகும். 

தமிழ் மக்கள் அமைதியை எவ்வளவு தூரம் நேசித்தார்கள் என்பதற்கும், தங்களின் தன்னாட்சி உரிமைக்காக எத்தகைய உன்னதமான தியாகங்களைச் செய்யத் துணிந்தார்கள் என்பதற்கும் நல்லூர் வீதி இன்றும் சாட்சியாக நிற்கிறது.

 ஜனாதிபதி அனுரகுமார திசாநாயக்கவின் புதிய அரசாங்கமும், தென்னிலங்கையின் வர்க்க இடதுசாரிகளும் தமிழ் மக்களின் தேசிய இனப் பிரச்சினையை வெறும் சலுகை அரசியலாகச் சுருக்க முயலும் இந்நாட்களில், திலீபனின் ஐந்து அம்சக் கோரிக்கைகள் என்பது ஈழத்தமிழர் தேசத்தின் இறைமை மற்றும் தன்னுரிமைக் கோட்பாடுகளுடன் பிணைக்கப்பட்டது என்ற சித்தாந்தப் புரிதல் அவசியமாகிறது. தமிழ்க் கட்சிகள்  நாடாளுமன்றத் தேர்தல் அதிகாரப் போட்டிகளில் வாக்கு வங்கிகளைச் சிதறடித்துக் கொண்டிருக்கும் பலவீனமான சூழலில், திலீபனின் தியாக நினைவுகள் மட்டுமே தமிழ் மக்களை ஒரு தேசிய இனமாக ஒன்றிணைக்கும் தார்மீகப் பின்விசையாகத் தொழிற்படுகிறது.

எனவே, உலகளாவிய தமிழ்த் தேசிய அரசியல் கோட்பாட்டின் தளத்தில் நின்று நாம் உள்வாங்க வேண்டிய உண்மை என்னவெனில், திலீபனின் நாமம் என்பது வெறும் கடந்த கால நினைவல்ல; அது எதிர்கால அரசியல் விடுதலைக்கான திசைகாட்டியாகும். 

திலீபனைப் பாடிட வார்த்தைகள் இல்லை என்றாலும், அவர் தன் மரணத்தின் மூலம் எழுதிச் சென்ற தத்துவார்த்தப் பிரகடனம் என்பது ஈழத்தமிழர் தேசத்தின் சுயநிர்ணய உரிமை ஒருபோதும் பேரப் பொருளாக மாற்றப்படக் கூடாது என்பதுதான். 

தென்னிலங்கை அரசுகளின் இராஜதந்திர மழுப்பல்களுக்கும், சர்வதேசப் புவிசார் அரசியல் போட்டிகளுக்கும் பலியாகாமல், செம்மணியின் மீளெழும் சாட்சியங்கள் மற்றும் திலீபன் போன்ற மாவீரர்களின் தியாக பலத்துடன், தாயக மண்ணின் இறையாண்மையைப் பாதுகாக்கும் அறிவுப்பூர்வமான சித்தாந்தப் பாதையை உலக அரங்கில் முன்னெடுப்பதே நாம் அந்தத் தியாக தீபத்திற்குச் செலுத்தும் உண்மையான தார்மீக மரியாதையாகும்.

text:
🇺🇸🧺 The giant laundromat that turned laundry into an experience

In Berwyn, Illinois, the World’s Largest Laundromat operates 24 hours a day with 140 washers and 170 dryers across roughly 14,000 square feet. Its size is only part of the story. The family business offers free coffee and donuts in the mornings, pizza on Wednesdays, a bird aviary, a children’s area and even visits from Santa during the winter. The Benson family has spent years making the hours families spend doing laundry more comfortable. That approach changes the role of the business, turning an ordinary household chore into a place where people can also spend time together. Its model shows how meeting a basic need while improving the experience can give an everyday business a genuine role in the community.

 GROK:"Teen with Aggressive Brain Tumor Shows No Evidence of Disease
Last updated 7 hours ago
After surgery by UCLA's Dr. Linda Liau removed 90 percent of a massive tumor, Braelyn received a personalized DCVax vaccine made from her preserved tumor tissue, along with radiation and Keytruda. The UCLA tumor board confirmed on recent scans that even the remaining 10 percent had vanished, leaving experts amazed and recommending they continue the plan. Her mother Amanda shared the joyful update, thanking supporters and stressing the need for better access to such treatments and routine tumor tissue preservation. Clinical trials back DCVax's survival benefits over standard care.
This story is a summary of posts on X and may evolve over time. Grok can make mistakes, verify its outputs."

@HollensbeAmanda·11hI have been waiting almost 3 years to write these words:  NO EVIDENCE OF DISEASE. 🙏❤️  Today we met with Braelyn’s neurosurgeon, Dr. Linda Liau at UCLA (telehealth).   When our local radiologist read Braelyn’s August 28 MRI as “no evidence of disease recurrence,” we were thrilled—but I was afraid to fully exhale.  I knew Dr. Liau and the UCLA tumor board would scrutinize every millimeter of those images.  What if they saw something the local radiologist missed?  Today, Dr. Liau told us that she and the tumor board had thoroughly reviewed Braelyn’s MRI.  They were amazed.  There is NO VISIBLE TUMOR.  Even the ~10% Dr. Liau had to leave behind during surgery because of its intimate involvement with critical structures is no longer visible.  She emphasized how amazed and pleased the entire tumor board was by such a complete response at this point.  Her assessment: the prior radiation and the ongoing DCVax appear to be working very well.  Their recommendation after also reviewing the Keytruda regimen Braelyn recently started?  KEEP DOING WHAT SHE’S DOING.  😭🙏  First and foremost, we give ALL thanks and glory to God.  People all over the world have prayed for this girl. I cannot begin to express how humbled and grateful we are.  But tonight I also cannot stop thinking about how close Braelyn came to never having this opportunity.  Earlier this year, her tumor was enormous and growing rapidly.  We sought help from multiple surgeons—including at prestigious institutions.  We were told further surgery was too risky.  We were offered the same old options: chemotherapy and photon radiation that would affect most of her brain, given the size of her tumor.   Her tumor is MGMT-unmethylated, so for Braelyn, chemo was all risk with little to no benefit.   And then a stranger I met here on X changed everything.@ThomasOwenMcCa1connected us with Dr. Liau.  After reviewing Braelyn’s case, one of the first things she said was:  “This girl needs surgery right away.”  I told her we knew that. We just couldn’t find anyone willing to do it.  I asked if SHE would.  “If you can get her to me, I will do her surgery.”  We got Braelyn to UCLA.  Within two weeks, Dr. Liau operated and removed ~90% of a massive tumor spanning three lobes, stopping where continuing would risk critical structures.  And this time, her tumor tissue was PROPERLY PRESERVED.  That tissue was ultimately sent to England and used to manufacture Braelyn’s personalized DCVax vaccine.  She has now received 3 induction doses + her first booster.  And today?  The tumor that Dr. Liau had to leave behind is no longer visible on MRI.  Think about that.  And then think about what could have happened if we had simply accepted “there’s nothing else we can do.”  THIS is why I will not stop advocating for reform.  Patients should not have to find potentially life-saving treatment options accidentally through strangers on social media.  Patients should be told about legitimate investigational options when standard treatment offers little hope.  Patients undergoing tumor surgery should be informed BEFORE surgery about preservation of tissue that could potentially be used for personalized treatments.  And patients should have the right to make informed decisions about which risks they are willing to take.  Promising science means very little if the patients who need it cannot access it.  Braelyn is living proof of why access matters.  Tonight, though, advocacy can wait for just a moment.  Tonight I’m her mom.  And I finally get to say the words I have begged God to someday let me say:  NO EVIDENCE OF DISEASE.  Thank You, God.  Thank you, Dr. Liau.  Thank you to everyone who opened a door, donated, shared her story, fought for her and prayed for our girl.  There is always light, even in the darkest places.  Tonight that light is shining incredibly bright. ❤️🙏  #DCVaxForBraelyn #CureNotCovered@greta@kshaughnessy2@andrewcaravello

By Ian Bradbury for The Bureau

Incidents like the 2022 Coastal GasLink attack, the December 2023 Ottawa plot against Jewish events and the January 2024 Edmonton City Hall attack underscore the stakes, yet they fade from public discourse without rigorous analysis. This is not mere oversight—it is a systemic failure of Canada’s counter-radicalization and extremism frameworks and media, exposing the nation to risks from under-assessed threats.
In June 2025, a former British Columbia civil liberties leader—forced to resign in 2021 for rhetoric deemed too extreme even by the province’s NDP government—re-emerged to lead a protest outside the Canada Border Services Agency offices in Vancouver. Her earlier praise of Hamas attackers’ hang-glider tactics as “beautiful” and her call to “burn it all down” amid the 2021 church arsons across Canada raise a critical question: Is this the sign of a deeper ideological current gaining momentum beneath the surface?
Canada faces a mounting crisis of radicalization and extremism, yet its citizens remain largely uninformed or, worse, misinformed.
Despite tens of millions invested in counter-radicalization over the past decade, threats from extremist elements within the Pro-Palestinian movement, the “Hands Off Iran” protests, and left-wing extremism receive insufficient scrutiny.
The “Hands Off Iran” demonstrations on June 22, 2025, which rallied hundreds in support of the Iranian regime—planned before U.S. strikes on Iranian nuclear facilities and organized by many of the same protest groups active since October 7, 2023—highlight this neglect.
The absence of detailed reporting obscures their scope and significance. Incidents like the January 2024 Edmonton City Hall attack and the December 2023 Ottawa plot against Jewish events underscore the stakes, yet they fade from public discourse without rigorous analysis.
This is not mere oversight—it is a systemic failure of Canada’s counter-radicalization and extremism frameworks and media, exposing the nation to risks from under-assessed threats.
Under-assessed Threats in Plain Sight
Pro-Palestinian rallies in Vancouver, Toronto, Ottawa, and Montreal reveal this gap. Flags of Hamas and Hezbollah—designated terrorist groups in Canada—have been displayed openly, and chants of “Death to Canada”, “Death to America”, and “Death to Israel, Death to Jews” have been reported, yet government-funded organizations offer no in-depth analysis of the radical networks or rhetoric tied to these events.
The “Hands Off Iran” protests face the same silence. Where are the detailed reports dissecting these movements? Where are the network maps or guides to their flags, symbols, and rhetoric, as seen for far-right groups?
Similarly, Left-wing accelerationism, an neo-marxist ideology advocating violent societal collapse, has fueled incidents like the 2022 Coastal GasLink attack, the 2021 church arsons, and anti-colonial criminal acts, yet it is overshadowed and downplayed by coverage of far-right threats, such as militant “right-wing accelerationism”. Two cases illustrate the broad urgency: the Edmonton attack, involving gunfire and a Molotov cocktail, included a video supporting Palestine and condemning Israel’s actions in Gaza, but was downplayed as “salad-bar extremism.”
The Ottawa plot, inspired by Islamic extremism and the Israel-Palestine conflict, vanished from headlines with alarming speed. These incidents demand thorough investigation, not dismissal.
A Counter-Radicalization Industry Misaligned
Canada’s counter-radicalization efforts fail to address the full spectrum of threats. Organizations such as the Canadian Centre for the Prevention of Radicalization Leading to Violence and the Canadian Anti-Hate Network (an organization linked to the extremist decentralized Antifa movement) focus heavily on far-right extremism and limited Islamic threats (e.g., ISIS and Al-Qaeda), while sidelining left-wing extremism, accelerationism, anarchist extremism, and broader Islamic,

Laughing with Mandelson. Anti-establishment? Pull the other one.

There he is. Nigel Farage. Mouth open. Champagne garden. Next to Peter Mandelson.

That is not a rebel in the wilderness. That is the club recognising itself.

Farage sells himself as the man against the machine. Brexit pint. Boats video. Punch-up with Labour over crypto cheques. Then the camera catches him at the US embassy’s Fourth of July do — Winfield House, summer 2025 — chuckling while Britain’s then Washington ambassador works the lawn. Same Mandelson who asked Starmer’s lot to use Farage as a “bridge” to Trump and Musk. Same Farage who offered to play that bridge for the “national interest.” Establishment talking to establishment. Different ties. Same room.

And Mandelson is not a random guest with a funny accent. He is New Labour royalty — twice resigned from Cabinet, forever back in the tent — until the Epstein files blew the door off. Bloomberg and the US document dumps showed a long friendship with Jeffrey Epstein that ran past the 2008 conviction: supportive emails, travel links, reports of time on Epstein’s jet. Bank statements later appeared to show tens of thousands flowing to Mandelson-linked accounts; he has said he has no record or recollection. Starmer sacked him as ambassador when the depth of that relationship became politically radioactive. The Met opened a criminal investigation into alleged misconduct in public office — market-sensitive material allegedly passed to Epstein while Mandelson was business secretary. That is the public record. Not a meme. Not a vibe.

So the question writes itself. Why does the “anti-establishment” tribune of Clacton share a laugh with a man that deep in the Epstein swamp? Because Farage was never outside the game. He is a face the system can use: split the right, talk boats without remigration, import Tory defectors, refuse a real pact with Rupert Lowe, then sip with Labour’s darkest operator when Washington needs a middleman.

I am Restore. Not Reform. Country first means leaving the ECHR, remigrating, one law — not networking the old order’s survivors on embassy grass. If your rebellion includes Peter Mandelson’s smile, it is not a rebellion. It is a career.

Restore Britain. Rupert Lowe. Keep the outsiders who stay outside.

The United States has criticized Canada over a modest electric vehicle deal with China.
🇨🇳Yet the U.S. itself once stabbed a loyal ally in the back and handed everything over to that very same China.
And, in less than two weeks, Trump will welcome a triumphant Xi to the White House—a leader emboldened by a hegemony he owes to a betrayal and a gift from the United States decades ago.

Here is the story and lesson from history.

🇹🇼The U.S. abandonment of the Republic of China (Taiwan) in 1979

After Mao’s revolution in 1949, Chiang Kai-shek’s Nationalists fled and took refuge on the island of Taiwan.

The United States offered them unwavering support, signing a mutual defense treaty in 1954 and deploying troops there.

They recognized only one legitimate government in China: Taiwan.

Everything changed in 1979.

In the midst of the Cold War, Washington sought to drive a wedge between the two major communist blocs—the USSR and China—fearing an alliance between them.

They also chose to share their technology with China, believing that giving the country a taste of capitalism and its wealth would set it on the path to democracy.

But China demanded a price for distancing itself from Moscow: abandoning Taiwan and formally recognizing Beijing.

Washington terminated all its treaties with Taiwan, leaving it diplomatically and militarily isolated—with only a flimsy protective measure in place: a treaty obliging the U.S. to sell Taiwan defensive weapons, but without any formal promise to defend the island.

Parallel with Canada

The U.S. is disregarding its signature on the USMCA free trade agreement, attempting to circumvent—or even violate—its legal terms. Its persistent attacks challenging Canada’s sovereignty—such as the push to rename Lake Ontario—and equating Canada with China by threatening to target its currency demonstrate that its word and signature hold weight only as long as it sees sufficient benefit in honoring them.

Long-term outlook regarding the break with Taiwan

Ultimately, the U.S. lost its gamble; China has moved closer to Russia and is financing its war in Ukraine. Furthermore, having absorbed the mechanics of capitalism, China never democratized. Leveraging its massive population and tools provided by the U.S., it has emerged as a primary political, military, and economic rival.

There is now near-unanimity among diplomatic, political, and economic experts in describing this decision as a monumental error:

“Our assumption that trade would bring political freedom was naive. We underestimated the Communist Party’s ability to absorb global capitalism while strengthening its totalitarian control.” — Winston Lord, ambassador and architect, alongside Henry Kissinger, of the opening to China.

“Allowing the massive transfer of industrial and scientific technologies to Beijing, while pretending to believe that China would remain a peaceful, secondary player, will go down in history as the worst act of self-sabotage ever committed by a superpower.” — Edward Luttwak, historian, political scientist, and grand strategy specialist.

text:
The Clarity Act. 

Want Community Banks to Thrive? Repeal Dodd-Frank and Pass CLARITY

We live in a political world where facts increasingly do not matter. Team Warren wants to kill the CLARITY Act, and no one should be surprised. The latest pretext is that community banks must be protected from digital asset competition, even as Washington’s own policies helped make it harder for community banks to survive.

America has lost roughly 3,100 community banks since Dodd-Frank became law. The number fell from about 7,000 in 2010 to 5,300 by 2017, and to fewer than 4,000 by the end of 2025. 

Most did not fail in a dramatic FDIC resolution. They merged, sold, or concluded that remaining independent no longer justified the regulatory cost.

Dodd-Frank did not create bank consolidation. But it accelerated it. Its sprawling compliance regime rewarded scale, giant banks can spread lawyers, compliance officers, reporting systems, and regulatory overhead across trillions of dollars in assets. A local lender cannot.

Now Team Warren and congressional Democrats appear prepared to block the CLARITY Act in the name of protecting consumers and community banks. 

But their approach would protect incumbents from competition, not communities from harm.

It is the same policy error Washington made in the 1970s. Regulation Q capped what banks could pay depositors. When inflation and market rates rose, money market funds offered savers better returns. Deposits flowed out of banks, not because money market funds were unfair, but because regulation made banks uncompetitive. The solution was not to outlaw competition. It was to dismantle the rules that prevented banks from competing.

That lesson matters today. 

Community banks will not be revived by blocking stablecoins or turning the CLARITY Act into another protectionist exercise. They need lower compliance costs, proportionate supervision, and freedom to compete for deposits.

If Democrats block clarity for digital assets while preserving the regulatory regime that hollowed out local banking, they will confirm a growing reality, this is an anti-innovation party. 

If Congress wants community banks to thrive, it should roll back Dodd-Frank’s small-bank burden and pass the CLARITY Act.

text:
$IONQ Xi's Great Wall of China Surrounds China's Quantum Physicists - New China Travel Ban Policy Highlights Nation's Serious Quantum Agenda as China's President Xi Prepares to Meet U.S. President Trump.

As of today, the People's Republic of China can lawfully prevent its own scientists from leaving the country on the grounds that their knowledge is too valuable to travel. State Council Decree No. 841, signed by Premier Li Qiang on July 22 and promulgated on July 31, took effect this morning. It runs nineteen articles and constitutes the most significant revision of China's border framework since the Exit and Entry Administration Law came into force in 2013. The provision that matters is not buried. Where a Chinese citizen violates rules on export control or technology import and export administration in a manner that may endanger national industrial or technological security, the competent departments of the State Council — the commerce authority among them — may decide that the individual shall not be permitted to leave the country. A separate clause allows bans of six months to three years for conduct abroad deemed to endanger national security and interests. The regulation also creates a notification procedure for exit bans, and then permits authorities to withhold that notification where a national security or criminal matter is involved. A scientist can be barred from a flight and, as a matter of published rule, need not be told why.

The reason this lands on quantum is that quantum is already inside the controlled perimeter. China's Catalogue of Technologies Prohibited or Restricted from Export, revised in December 2023 and updated since, added cryptographic security technologies and laser technologies to the restricted list, and China's quantum-specific export controls run to licensing for quantum cryptography and cryogenic components. That places a substantial fraction of the country's quantum workforce — the cryptography people, the laser and ion-trap people, the dilution refrigerator and cryogenic supply chain people — inside a category the new exit provisions explicitly reach. A physicist does not need to have done anything to be affected; the relevant machinery is discretionary, administered by commerce and public security authorities rather than courts, and calibrated by the state to whatever the state decides industrial security requires on a given morning. The official framing is that this decree exists to protect rare earth processing and battery manufacturing know-how, and Western coverage has dutifully reported it that way. I do not accept that reading, and neither should anyone who has watched how Beijing packages its most consequential moves. Rare earths are the wrapper. They are the legible, commercially plausible cover story, the version a foreign correspondent can file without alarming an editor, the version that makes a border overhaul sound like industrial housekeeping. Look instead at how the instrument is actually built. Its operative trigger names no industry at all — it is violation of export control and technology import and export rules in a manner that may endanger industrial or technological security. That means the decree's real perimeter is set by the catalogue, and the catalogue is a document the State Council controls and has revised repeatedly, adding cryptographic security technologies, laser technologies and information countermeasure technologies as it went. A rule whose scope is defined by an internal list the rulemaker can amend at will is not a rule about rare earths. It is a rule about whatever Beijing decides tomorrow that it is about. Then weigh the proportionality. Nineteen articles, drafted on an urgent-priority basis, amounting to the largest reconstruction of China's exit regime in thirteen years. No state rebuilds its border framework at that scale to stop battery technicians from taking consulting work abroad. Weigh the notification clause, which lets authorities withhold the reason for a ban where national security or a criminal investigation is involved — that is a counterintelligence provision, not a trade secrets provision. Weigh the timing, arriving as the Fifteenth Five-Year Plan names quantum among its strategic targets and as the artificial intelligence race enters its most consequential year. This is a quantum and AI scientist prohibition wrapped in another package. Naming those two fields in the text would have told the world exactly what China believes those programs are worth; naming rare earths costs Beijing nothing and delivers the thing Xi prizes above all, which is a decisive instrument that arrives looking unremarkable. The open hand stays extended in public — the collaboration invitations, the conference keynotes, the cooperative language offered to European capitals — while the exit door quietly acquires a lock. What changed today is not rhetoric but capability. Beijing now holds a clean, published, administratively simple mechanism for keeping its quantum and AI talent inside the wall, and instruments of that kind are not built to go unused.

Which brings us to the argument now consuming Washington and Silicon Valley. On September 12, Dario Amodei published "We Must Pace the Frontier," arguing that the industry should deliberately slow the rate at which model capabilities improve — not halt training or releases, he was explicit about that, but build in time for alignment work and third-party verification. Sam Altman agreed within hours, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis followed, and by Monday AI-linked equities were selling off and the President was criticizing Amodei by name, with the Vice President warning that regulation would weaken America's hand against Beijing. Reasonable people can hold either position, and Amodei's is not the naive one — he has simultaneously pushed for tighter chip controls on China, which puts him closer to the administration on the competitive question than the headlines allow. But set the merits aside and look at the sequencing. In the same week that American frontier labs debated a voluntary brake, the Chinese state implemented a rule that makes it harder for its own AI and quantum engineers to board an international flight. One system is deliberating about slowing down. The other is bolting down its people. Whatever one concludes about safety governance, no one should pretend these two weeks produce a symmetric outcome, and in a technology race where the winner sets the standards, controls the supply chain and reads everyone else's mail, second place is last place.

The deeper problem is that the American debate is being conducted against a Chinese capability estimate that China itself supplies. Xi Jinping has never shown more than a little of what is in his cup. That is method, not accident. Adversaries are permitted to see a measured amount, they rationalize a ceiling from it, they build planning assumptions on that ceiling, and then they discover there are a dozen more cups nobody had counted. He rebuilt a country this way while the rest of the world explained why he could not. XI SHOWS YOU ONE CUP BUT HIDES 12 CUPS. THAT'S HIS WAY. AND THIS IS HOW HE REBUILT CHINA. 

Applied to quantum, the pattern is consistent and the evidence fits: a program that has run behind a wall since roughly the era China was shut out of the International Space Station and built its own instead; capability that matures inside provincial and national laboratories, state-owned defense primes and military-civil fusion structures; and commercial visibility that appears only when internal growth overflows what those closed channels can absorb. The venture rounds Western analysts are now tabulating — the state-owned defense conglomerate leading a pre-IPO round, the provincial platforms filling out the book — are not the beginning of China's quantum push. They are the spillover from something older and larger, surfacing because it now needs open-market capital and open-market hiring. Every Chinese quantum figure in circulation today is therefore a floor of unknown distance from the real number, which means the honest assessment is not that China is behind, or level, or ahead. It is that China's program is very likely more advanced than the visible record can support, that nobody outside can size it, and that the exit rules taking effect today are one more brick in the wall that keeps it that way.

If the response to all of this cannot be to stop building — and it cannot — then it has to be to build the layer underneath. That is where @IonQ_Inc 's position becomes strategically more important than most people realize rather than merely commercially interesting, and it is the thesis I set out at length in Part IV of this series, IonQ and the Infrastructure Beneath the AI Transition that I expect to release today. 

The AI problems currently dominating the press are infrastructure problems wearing application clothing. Power is the first: IonQ's July 2026 work with QuantumBasel identified an energy break-even near 34 qubits, above which quantum fine-tuning of certain AI workloads consumes less energy than the classical equivalent, aimed squarely at data center operators staring down a demand curve that classical scaling cannot serve. Security is the second: the agent-era failure mode is not an impostor but coordinated agents holding valid credentials, which makes key custody, quantum-safe key distribution and verifiable hardware provenance the actual control surface — and IonQ holds commercial standing across networking, key distribution and, through SkyWater's DMEA-accredited trusted foundry, domestic fabrication provenance that almost nobody else in the sector can claim. Both map directly onto stated White House priorities: Executive Order 14412's post-quantum cryptography migration deadlines, Executive Order 14413's quantum pillars spanning computing, sensing, networking, supply chain and workforce, and the Genesis Mission's explicit coupling of AI capability to American energy dominance. The administration's position is that America must not slow down. Fine. Then the only coherent policy is to fund the substrate that lets it go fast safely — the energy, the cryptography, the trusted silicon, the networks — because that is the one part of this race where the United States still holds a durable lead, and it is the one part Beijing cannot wall off, conceal, or keep from boarding a plane.

In no short order when we think about the issues I have shared here, and understanding the risks that are at stake, I realize with a sense of gratitude that @NiccoloDeMasi had the insight and determination to build IonQ's full stake platform.

I lived in Oregon for 25 years, up until 2024.  Kotek's insane taxes are killing small business and driving large employers out of the state in droves.  She got a "corporate activity" tax passed that is 3% of every dollar of gross business income.  That's on top of 8% income tax on any profit I make.  It was an end run around the voters who wouldn't approve a sales tax.  So now, if your profit margin was already small, like under 5%, you're out of business.  

They wonder why rent is through the roof, while property taxes are insane.  My 2100 sf house there was $6,000 per year in property taxes.  That's $500 per month.  That's a business expense I have to recover if I rent it out.  

Anti-growth land use laws prevent new housing from being built, but Kotek cries about the housing shortage.  Here in the Midwest I have a dozen new subdivisions being built within 3 miles of my house.  That's hundreds of new houses per year in a town of 35,000 people.  I can't EVER remember seeing a new subdivision under construction in Oregon.  Planning and permits for a new house can run in the range of $40,000, and take years to get approved.  Construction costs are above $300 per square foot, making a basic 2,000 sf house cost $600,000 or more.

Enivironmental laws have killed the main rural industry, timber.  Small towns throughout rural Oregon, (about 95% of the state) are dead or dying.  The only industries left are tourism, Social Security, and Welfare.  Small rural communities are now largely populated with retirees, disabled, and drug addicts.

The state is run primarily by three counties, Multnomah County (Portland), and Lane County (Eugene), and Benton County (Corvallis).  Each of these counties harbors a major university with at least 30,000 students each.  These 90,000 voters, in a state with an active voting population of 2,000,000 constitute about 5% of the vote.  These naive voters are easily manipulated into voting as a block.  Multnomah County, with 70% of active voters in the state, votes nearly 80% Democrat.  Oregon is a one party state.  They haven't had a Republican governor in 40 years.

And those large employers who are leaving or have left?

Headquarters that left the state

Dutch Bros — official HQ from Grants Pass to Phoenix. Roasting/support stays in Grants Pass; corporate jobs shifted to Arizona.

Tektronix — Beaverton HQ moved to Raleigh, N.C. after a change in ownership (announced 2025). Historic Oregon tech name.

JELD-WEN — corporate HQ from Klamath Falls to North Carolina; later closed the Chiloquin factory (~128 jobs).

Bowtech Archery — Eugene HQ/manufacturing to Houston (2026); ~43 jobs. Smaller than the others, still a full exit.

Still in Oregon, but big cuts or a site gone

Intel — still the state’s largest private employer and still in Hillsboro/Aloha, but it shed on the order of 6,000+ Oregon jobs from 2024–2025. Local headcount fell from ~23,000 toward the mid-teens of thousands. Not a departure; a deep retreat.

Daimler Truck — ending truck manufacturing in Portland (~375 jobs), production to the Carolinas; North American HQ stays in Portland.

Wells Fargo — pulling global-operations offices out of Hillsboro, Portland, and Salem (2025); branches remain. Hundreds of back-office jobs offered relocation out of state.

Salesforce — closed Hillsboro office; relocate, go remote, or take severance.

Nike — HQ still Beaverton; hundreds of local jobs cut in restructuring, not an exit.

KEEN — closed Swan Island factory. Adobe left its SW 1st Ave Portland office. REI closed the Pearl co-op (retail, not HQ).

◾ Oman is the only Gulf state that has maintained long-standing friendly relations with Iran.
◾Oman secretly facilitated the US-Iran nuclear negotiations in 2013, which ultimately led to the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA).
◾In 2026, Oman hosted the Salalah Conference involving Iran, the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Iraq to discuss new shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz.
◾ Oman serves as the "Swiss channel" for passing messages between Iran and the US yet it is more credible than Switzerland, given the shared strategic waterway and centuries of neighborly relations between Oman and Iran.

When Rubio picked up the phone, who else could he call?

◾Saudi Arabia? Trump has already twice rejected the Saudi Crown Prince's requests for military aid. Saudi Arabia is currently requesting intelligence from Israel via CENTCOM.  · Qatar? Qatar maintains diplomatic relations with Iran, but it also hosts the forward headquarters of U.S. Central Command. Iran does not trust Qatar.
◾ Iraq? The Iraqi government is preparing for "Sovereignty Day" on September 30 and is expelling U.S. forces. Iran wields immense influence in Iraq, but Iraq is not a "middleman"—it is a "battlefield."
◾ Türkiye? Türkiye is a NATO member, yet Erdoğan maintains energy and trade ties with Iran. However, Türkiye itself is facing U.S. sanctions (related to Golden Global Bank), and U.S.-Turkiye relations are strained.

◾Oman. Only Oman.

Rubio’s phone call served as a "strategic tourniquet" for the U.S. after Iran put a stranglehold on the Strait of Hormuz.

🛢️On September 13, 2026, Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi announced a fact completely overlooked by Western media during an interview with *The New Arab*:

"The understanding reached with Oman in no way implies the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s condition for reopening the strait is that the U.S. must return to honoring the commitments of the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding."

Araghchi’s statement was unequivocal: Iran and Oman have reached an agreement on new shipping lanes for the Strait of Hormuz. The route entering the Persian Gulf lies "entirely within Iranian territorial waters." The route exiting the Persian Gulf lies "partially within Iranian territorial waters." The southern route will be closed. The map has been drawn. The documents are ready for submission to the International Maritime Organization.

What does this mean?

The U.S. Navy’s Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain was destroyed by Iran. U.S. forces were forced to retreat to Diego Garcia, thousands of kilometers away. The U.S. claims to "control the Strait of Hormuz." Iran has proven through its actions who actually holds that control.

Rubio called Oman not to "discuss regional developments," but to attempt through Oman to get Iran to reopen a shipping lane that the U.S. Navy could use.

But Araghchi’s condition was clear: the U.S. must return to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. This means lifting the maritime blockade.  Return frozen assets. Lift oil sanctions. Halt all actions justified by threats or military maneuvers.

Can Rubio accept these conditions? If he does, the entire U.S. military architecture in the Middle East will collapse. If he refuses, the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed.

🇾🇪The second reason for Rubio’s call to Oman was Yemen.

Yemeni armed forces seized control of the entire Red Sea coastline within 18 hours. They captured the port of Mocha and Perim Island. They gained full control of the Strait of Bab al-Mandab. They took the Jabal Kahboub mountain range, the high ground overlooking the strait. They captured 1,500 Saudi mercenaries and seized equipment belonging to 30 military brigades.

The Saudi East-West Pipeline the only alternative route bypassing the Strait of Hormuz was shut down. Pumping stations were destroyed; repairs would take five to six weeks. Inventories at the port of Yanbu were sufficient for only five to seven days.

Saudi Arabia appealed to the U.S. for help. Trump refused twice. Saudi Arabia then turned to Israel for intelligence.

Rubio’s call to Oman was an attempt to find a "graceful exit," a way for Saudi Arabia to save face while halting the advance of the Yemeni armed forces.

However, Iran’s conditions were: lift the blockade on Yemen; stop the aggression against Yemen; and recognize the legitimacy of the Yemeni armed forces.

Can Rubio accept these conditions?

🇮🇶 The third reason concerns Iraq.

September 30, 2026, is the "fixed and final" deadline for the complete withdrawal of U.S. troops from Iraq. Iraqi military spokesman Sabah al-Numan announced: "September 30 will be Iraq's Sovereignty Day."

The U.S. has stationed troops in Iraq for over 20 years. It does not want to leave.

Yet, Iran wields immense influence in Iraq.  Pro-Iran factions within the Iraqi parliament, the Badr Organization, the Fatah Alliance, and the Sadrist Movement control the government. The Islamic Resistance in Iraq is launching attacks on U.S. military bases. The Iraqi government is coordinating border security with Iran.

Rubio’s call to Oman was likely an attempt to convey a message to Iran via Oman: Could the Iraqi government "slow down" its demands for a U.S. troop withdrawal? Could the Islamic Resistance in Iraq "pause" its attacks on U.S. forces?

However, Iran’s terms are clear: U.S. forces must fully withdraw from Iraq. Iraq’s sovereignty is non-negotiable.

💀Rubio faced a fundamental problem when calling Oman: he had nothing to offer Iran.

Iran’s conditions are clear:

◾ Lift the naval blockade on Iran.
◾Return frozen Iranian assets.
◾Lift sanctions on Iranian oil exports.
◾ Cease all actions justified by threats or military maneuvers.
◾Recognize Iran’s jurisdiction over the Strait of Hormuz.

Can the United States accept these terms?

If accepted, the U.S. military presence in the Middle East would lose its legitimacy. The Fifth Fleet would be unable to return to Bahrain. The Strait of Hormuz would be jointly managed by Iran and Oman. Yemeni armed forces would retain control over the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Iraq would expel U.S. troops. The entire U.S. security architecture in the Middle East would collapse.

If not accepted, Rubio’s call remains merely a "conversation" yielding no results, no agreements, and no breakthroughs.

Oman’s statement spoke of an "exchange of views." Translated, this means: Rubio stated his position; Oman stated Iran’s position. No agreement was reached between the parties.

text:
💎 MY FAVORITE STOCK PITCH FROM YESTERDAY

$SPWH, written up by Benevolus at The Illiquid Edge

Sportsman's Warehouse is priced for bankruptcy, and none of its debt comes due until 2031.

147 hunting, fishing and outdoor stores in 32 states, mostly in the Western US. $1.16 a share at Monday's close, and about $220m buys the whole business including its debt.

WHY PEOPLE WALK IN
Guns and ammunition sell at everyday low prices and thin margins. A customer legally has to come into the store to buy a firearm, and while there adds the boots, gloves and camping gear that carry the margin. Benevolus shops exactly like that, forgetting new boots until standing in the store picking up ammunition and a hunting license. Hunting and shooting was 66.4% of sales in the quarter to May 2.

WHAT WENT WRONG
Covid sent everyone outdoors and profits hit records. The chain spent them opening stores and stocking up, overbuilt both, and same store sales kept falling into 2026. They have now leveled off. Back in late 2020 there was an $18 a share takeover offer, which fell apart on antitrust grounds.

THE BANKRUPTCY CHECK
Its loans are secured on its assets, mostly inventory, with no major covenants. The main one is tied to 10% of that asset base, about $30m, and there is $80m of borrowing left before it trips. Suppliers are not asking to be paid any faster, so they do not seem to see a bankruptcy coming either.

For the floor, Benevolus went through the inventory category by category against what bankrupt peers like Gander Mountain got for theirs, assuming a liquidator recovers 100% on ammunition, 95% on firearms and 80 to 85% on the rest. An orderly liquidation comes out at $0.77 a share, about a third under Monday's price.

THE UPSIDE
Before covid the business made $63m of EBITDA, roughly cash operating profit, on 92 stores. Benevolus estimates $75m on 140. Take off $25m of maintenance capex, shelter the rest with roughly $85m of past losses that offset federal tax, and normalized free cash flow is about $50m a year.

"Put another way we are paying $220mn for an enterprise that can do $50mn in FCF, or 4.5x."

At a 12.5% yield, less debt, that makes $4.55 a share, 3.9x Monday's close.

WHAT TURNS IT
US gun sales have fallen every year since 2020, from 22.7M to an estimated 15.5M in 2025. Sales usually spike in an election year and Benevolus expects 2028 to do it, with the extra foot traffic running through stores carrying a lot of fixed cost.

Customers now pay online and pick up in store, which locks in the cheap ammunition before they walk in, and adding boots is harder once you have already paid. So the website was rebuilt to push bundles, and the CEO, who came from Cabela's, is reworking the loyalty program.

The company only has to stay cash flow neutral until the gun cycle turns, and it has until 2031 to wait. Benevolus finds it compelling here, and put it in the title: "Too cheap to ignore."

text:
I lived in Oregon for 25 years, up until 2024.  Governor Kotek's insane taxes are killing small business and driving large employers out of the state in droves.  She got a "corporate activity" tax passed that is 3% of every dollar of gross business income.  That's on top of 8% income tax on any profit I make.  It was an end run around the voters who wouldn't approve a sales tax.  So now, if your profit margin was already small, like under 5%, you're out of business.

Residents wonder why rent is through the roof, while property taxes are insane.  My 2100 sf house there was $6,000 per year in property taxes.  That's $500 per month.  That's a business expense I have to recover if I rent it out.

Anti-growth land use laws prevent new housing from being built, but Kotek cries about the housing shortage.  Here in the Midwest I have a dozen new subdivisions being built within 3 miles of my house.  That's hundreds of new houses per year in a town of 35,000 people.  I can't EVER remember seeing a new subdivision under construction in Oregon.  Planning and permits for a new house can run in the range of $40,000, and take years to get approved.  Construction costs are above $300 per square foot, making a basic 2,000 sf house cost $600,000 or more.

Environmental laws have killed the main rural industry, timber.  Small towns throughout rural Oregon, (about 95% of the state) are dead or dying.  The only industries left are tourism, Social Security, and Welfare.  Small rural communities are now largely populated with retirees, disabled, and drug addicts.

The state is run primarily by three counties, Multnomah County (Portland), and Lane County (Eugene), and Benton County (Corvallis).  Each of these counties harbors a major university with at least 30,000 students each.  These 90,000 voters, in a state with an active voting population of 2,000,000 constitute about 5% of the vote.  These naive voters are easily manipulated into voting as a block.  Multnomah County, with 70% of active voters in the state, votes nearly 80% Democrat.  Oregon is a one party state.  They haven't had a Republican governor in 40 years.

And those large employers who are leaving or have left?

Headquarters that left the state

Dutch Bros — official HQ from Grants Pass to Phoenix. Roasting/support stays in Grants Pass; corporate jobs shifted to Arizona.

Tektronix — Beaverton HQ moved to Raleigh, N.C. after a change in ownership (announced 2025). Historic Oregon tech name.

JELD-WEN — corporate HQ from Klamath Falls to North Carolina; later closed the Chiloquin factory (~128 jobs).

Bowtech Archery — Eugene HQ/manufacturing to Houston (2026); ~43 jobs. Smaller than the others, still a full exit.

Still in Oregon, but big cuts or a site gone

Intel — still the state’s largest private employer and still in Hillsboro/Aloha, but it shed on the order of 6,000+ Oregon jobs from 2024–2025. Local headcount fell from ~23,000 toward the mid-teens of thousands. Not a departure; a deep retreat.

Daimler Truck — ending truck manufacturing in Portland (~375 jobs), production to the Carolinas; North American HQ stays in Portland.

Wells Fargo — pulling global-operations offices out of Hillsboro, Portland, and Salem (2025); branches remain. Hundreds of back-office jobs offered relocation out of state.

Salesforce — closed Hillsboro office; relocate, go remote, or take severance.

Nike — HQ still Beaverton; hundreds of local jobs cut in restructuring, not an exit.

text:
Reading your other posts, I can tell you're a cerebral guy.  I'm going to assume you geek out on the analytical side of football.  So as the owner of an analytics consultancy, I'll offer you a pretty detailed thought-analysis on how last season's CFP rankings would've played out had Texas played a gimme P4 team in Week 1 (as the preseason #1) instead of Ohio St.  You can war game it and see that Texas would've easily been in had they finished 10-2.  Give it a read.  I think you'll agree.  Texas would've been the 7th or 8th seed in the playoffs.

Week 10
* Nov 1 -- Texas beat Vanderbilt
* Nov 4 -- 1st CFP Poll revealed.

Had Texas played a beatable P4 team in Week 1, they'd have been 8-1 heading into the 1st CFP poll, with a dominating win over Oklahoma, and just days removed from a big win over a Vandy squad that debuted at #16 in the 1st CFP poll. The other 1-loss teams in the 1st poll were:

#4 Alabama (7-1)
#5 Georgia (7-1)
#6 Ole Miss (8-1)
#8 TX Tech (8-1)
#9 Oregon (7-1)

Texas would've debuted in the 1st CFP poll in the Top 10....likely in the Top 8 (b/c they'd have far better wins than Tech or Oregon).

Week 11
* Texas had a bye
* #8 TX Tech blew out #7 BYU. No other Top 10 team lost. Tech moved up to #6, Ole Miss dropped to #7, and Oregon dropped to #8.
* Expected CFP Poll: Texas would've stayed in the 4-8 range. Tech likely wouldn't have moved ahead w/ only 1 good win vs 2 for Texas.

Week 12
* Texas blown out by #5 Georgia
* #11 Oklahoma beats #4 Alabama by 2 in a slopfest
* At this point, Texas, OU, and Alabama would all be 8-2, with Texas holding a head-to-head win over OU. The 8-2 teams in the resulting CFP poll were #8 OU, #9 Notre Dame, #10 Alabama, #12 Utah, #13 Miami, #14 Vandy.
* Expected CFP Poll: With wins over OU & Vandy, Texas almost certainly lands in the 8-10 range.

Week 13
* Texas destroyed Arkansas
* Oklahoma limped by Mizzou (17-6)
* #7 Oregon blew out #15 USC
* Everyone else played FCS/G5 teams
* Expected CFP Poll: Texas would've stayed in the 8-10 range.

Week 14
* Texas dominated #3 A&M
* #8 OU limped by LSU (17-13)
* #9 ND dominated Stanford
* #10 Alabama needed a miracle fumble at the end of the game to hang onto a W vs sub-.500 Auburn
* Expected CFP Poll: On the heels of a dominating W over #3 A&M, 10-2 Texas would've had a better resume than #8 OU, #9 Alabama, and #10 ND. A&M fell to #7. At 11-1, it's possible that A&M would've been dropped below Texas in that poll, resulting in Texas #7 and A&M #8. At worst though, Texas would be #8 in the final regular season CFP poll

Week 15
* #10 Alabama was blown out by #3 Georgia
* Texas, A&M, Notre Dame, Oklahoma, & Miami all sat at home.
* Expected CFP Poll: Texas would've remained #7 or #8. Absolutely 0% chance 10-2 Texas would've been ranked behind 10-2 Oklahoma or 10-3 Alabama.

Had Texas played a beatable team in Week 1, they'd have been in the CFP as the 7-seed or 8-seed, b/c under no circumstances (especially given how OU played the last month of the season) would the committee put 10-2 Texas behind 10-2 Oklahoma. So the only consideration is whether the CFP committee would have moved 11-1 A&M behind 10-2 Texas after getting dominated by them in the last game of the regular season.

text:
MICRON $MU IS BID BEFORE THE OPEN. THE BOARD IT SITS IN IS NOT:

Micron Technology at $934.61 (premarket), +$10.58 / +1.14% from Monday's $924.03 close. The Boise, Idaho company has made memory chips since 1978 - the chips that hold data while a computer is working on it - and on Monday it was one of the hardest-hit names on the American market.

The verdict this morning: Monday's damage came from an argument, not from a number, and the names it hit hardest are the ones bidding back while the wider board still leans lower. Nobody has finished deciding what the argument is worth.

US index futures - contracts on where an index finishes later, and the only live opinion while American shares are shut - are slightly offered ninety minutes before the bell:

- S&P 500 futures 7,678.25, -14.50 pts / -0.19%
- Nasdaq-100 futures 29,406.75, -42.75 pts / -0.15%
- Dow futures 52,704.00, -157 pts / -0.30%

Small numbers. What sits underneath them is not.

On Saturday, September 12, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei published an essay titled "We Must Pace the Frontier", arguing that AI labs should slow the rate at which they make their models more capable, because the safety work is not keeping up. The heads of OpenAI, Google DeepMind and xAI all agreed within a day. Elon Musk's reply ran to three words: "Dario is right." On Monday morning Amodei posted a longer version setting out how it would work in practice.

The people who would have to do the slowing all said yes. That is what moved a market on a day when no company reported anything.

Micron opened Monday at $906.03, a full $69.23 under Friday's $975.26 close - the selling was done before the bell rang. It finished at $924.03, down $51.23 / -5.25% on the day, but $18.00 above where it opened and $21.43 off its low. Volume was 27.1M shares against a 26.1M average. An ordinary number of shares changed hands on the worst day the chip names have had in months. Nobody ran. They repriced and stayed.

Here is why this name is the sharp end of that argument. In the three months to May 28, reported June 24, Micron kept 84.6 cents of every sales dollar after the cost of making the product - its gross margin. A year earlier it kept 39.0 cents. Revenue was $41.46B against $9.30B, +346%; net income $28.24B, or $24.67 a diluted share. It was the fifth quarterly revenue record in a row.

Almost none of those 45 extra cents came from Micron learning to build chips more cheaply. They came from the price of memory - a price Micron does not set. An argument about slowing AI down is an argument about how much memory gets bought and what it costs, which points it straight at the part of this company that changed.

Micron sits eleventh of thirty on the Hypergrowth Len5 watch, which looks for a business that is early as well as fast. Fast is not arguable at +346%. Early is what holds it down the list: a firm founded in 1978 employing 53,000 people is not early, and its longer record runs the other way, losing years included. Eleventh rather than nearer the top is that tension - one extraordinary year against a decade that contradicts it. CHANGE IT: units doing the work instead of price, which is visible on September 30, when the company's own map of about $50B of revenue has to arrive without the margin giving way.

SanDisk at $1,571.00 (premarket), +$19.01 / +1.23% from Monday's $1,551.99 close, is the same trade with a receipt attached. The Milpitas, California maker of flash storage - the memory that keeps data once the power is off - reported on August 5 that revenue rose 51% in three months to $8.97B, and said outright where it came from: roughly two thirds higher prices, one third selling more. It fell 4.98% Monday in the same selling, and it is tenth of thirty on that same Hypergrowth Len5 on the size and speed of that revenue base - the one name here that has already published the split the whole sector is now being repriced on.

Europe is having a quieter version of this. London closed Monday at 10,697.57, +47.17 pts / +0.44% - green, on the day American chip names were marked down hardest - and Frankfurt at 25,440.81, -128 pts / -0.50%. Neither has produced anything resembling Micron's Monday. For now this reads as an American repricing rather than a global rethink.

Two dated items frame the rest of the week, and the caveat comes first: an overnight lean is a thin crowd trading, and a move this small dies at the 9:30am open more often than it survives. The Federal Reserve begins a two-day meeting today and announces Wednesday at 2:00pm ET. Then Friday is quadruple witching - stock-index futures and options and single-stock options all expire the same day, with the S&P 500 quarterly rebalance effective at the close. Volume will be heavy for mechanical reasons, most of it positions being closed rather than opinions being formed. It is the worst day of the quarter to read a breakout.

WATCH the gross margin, not the revenue line. Revenue can hold up on volume while the price of memory slips, and the margin is where that shows first. WHEN: Wednesday, September 30, after the close, with Micron's own map at about $50B of revenue and roughly $31 a share. RISK: the stock is already 25.5% under the $1,255.00 it reached on June 25, so this was being marked down well before anyone wrote an essay.

Micron has set five revenue records in a row and still trades near 22 times earnings - the multiple of a company nobody expects to do it a sixth time. Over the weekend the four people who run the biggest AI labs agreed, in public, to go slower. On September 30 the company that sells them the memory has to say whether any of them has.

Not investment advice.
