BEGS AMERICA SAVE 6,000,000 IN RUSSIA
Massacre Threatens All Jews as Soviet Power Wanes, Declares Kreinin, Coming Here for Aid.

Copyright, 1921, by The Chicago Tribune Co.
BERLIN, July 19.—Russia’s 6,000,000 Jews are facing extermination by massacre. As the famine is spreading, the counter-revolutionary movement is gaining and the Soviet’s control is waning. This statement is borne out by official documents presented to the Berlin Government, which show that numerous pogroms are raging in all parts of Russia and the Ukraine.
The information was gathered by Dr. Joseph Kreinin, a noted Jewish social worker and President of the Russian Joint Board of Jewish Societies. He says that several villages have been burned already and scores killed, seventy in one village alone. He is en route to America, where he plans meetings in New York, Chicago and elsewhere for the purpose of “saving his people.”
According to Dr. Kreinin, mass flights from Russia have already begun, the Jews rushing to all borders and especially to Rumania, where there are 40,000 families camping along the frontier, hoping to find refuge. Among these, he says, at least 100 persons daily are dying from exposure and hunger.
Dr. Kreinin, who recently escaped from Moscow, says the pogroms are especially severe in the provinces of Homel, Minsk and Volhynia. The pogroms originated outside of Russia, in the Ukraine and White Russia.
He says in the Volga region a new sort of pogrom occurred, when Russian peasants attacked German settlements because they were foreigners. He declares the recent transfer of General Budenny into White Russia was for the purpose of pacifying the region.
“My object in visiting Germany and the United States is to organize all relief organizations throughout the world, Jewish as well as others,” he added. “The only hope for the millions of Jews is for American aid, both material and political.
“I cannot expect much effect from any political steps, as the Soviets are losing control everywhere except in the cities. The massacres are occurring chiefly in the small towns.
“However, I hope the American Government will realize the danger of massacres is greater than at any time in history, and I hope they will help open the borders and lift restrictions on entering the United States.”

The race for Colorado State Treasurer centers on how the state manages and invests its $17 billion in tax revenues. While traditionally a lower-profile administrative role, candidates Kevin Grantham (R) and Jeff Bridges (D) offer contrasting philosophies for the office:  

Kevin Grantham (R): Advocates keeping the treasurer's office focused on core duties—maximizing traditional safe-haven investments, improving efficiency for returning unclaimed property, and using the office's platform to advocate against excess state spending. 

Jeff Bridges (D): Proposes expanding the office's scope by directing a portion of state funds into local affordable housing and infrastructure projects, alongside creating a forensic auditing division to oversee spending across state agencies, and introduces mechanisms for corruption and cronyism.

text:
Last week I attended GFF one of the world's largest fintech gatherings, with 50,000+ attendees including the PM of India, the Finance Minister, Maharashtra's CM, and CXOs from every major Indian bank.

Here are my 14 observations:

1. Crypto and blockchain presence was minimal; the word "cryptocurrency" itself is avoided almost entirely

2. Everything gets called tokenization instead; tokenization was one of the key themes of the event

3. Tokenization here mostly means private bonds and private credit instruments, run in closed systems, not interoperable with the public blockchain world

4. Talked with several bond issuers and credit issuers, all building in these closed, permissioned setups

5. In the panels, policymakers and government chiefs actively avoided the term cryptocurrency; even major panel discussions centered on AI & fintech

6. Whenever tokenization came up on panels, it was framed as piloting DLTs and closed ledger systems, not public chains

7. There is a real lack of awareness across the system about what public blockchains like Ethereum actually offer

8. Almost nothing on privacy, security, or zero knowledge proofs and what they bring to financial infrastructure

9. There's no awareness between scammy crypto tokens and neutral infrastructure like Ethereum that provides rails for innovation and delivers net good to society

10. Stablecoins and tokenized assets represent $330B+ globally, but there's very little interest in that data point since Indian Institutions are not yet open for interoperable infra & public chains

11. Direct, dedicated engagement with policymakers and lawmakers is needed to show why public blockchains and privacy tech don't endanger citizens, and instead open up new opportunity and improve financial infrastructure

12. Conversations with SEBI, RBI innovation team, NPCI, and others confirmed no active public blockchain development yet, just early tinkering

13. Despite the bureaucracy, some internal teams within these orgs are surprisingly open and receptive to Ethereum's CROPS value proposition

14. AI agents were a dominant build theme across projects and booths (inspite of a fin-tech conf)

These are my ground-level observations from GFF. 

Over the past few months, while working at @EFDevcon, I got to connect with quite a few people working closely with Indian government bodies and institutions on tokenization, Ethereum, and public + private blockchains. 

Currently working on a report with @RohitMalekar, @rashmivabbigeri, and @denverjude. Hoping to publish soon and give you all a sneak peek on the state of institutional crypto in India.

text:
As a graduate student and a post doc I can relate to this experience.
We are so pushed to generate data towards something we can publish and get grants. And if the idea could land in a high impact gator journal you become the darling of the lab and the professor will do anything to make your future career the best it can be.
So most people fall into that .., sometimes we are pushed to generate things even when we see negative data because the professor likes the theory, wha scientists can do working in the wee night hours with no sleep due to stress and obligations and fear is a bit crazy but also not something we have not heard of,

I got lucky. I found a field that was open and the money needed to generate the data was minimal. I also had a habit of repeating the experiment 5 times. 3 by me and 2 by another lab tech or grad student or post doc. I offer them authorship in return. This reduces artifacts and that fear that I could be making something up. Apart from that I used 3-4 separate techniques to show the same result. For example if it’s cell division I am looking at I used immuno staining, flow cytometry, histology, brdu staining and several others to get the same result. This repetition helps to remove artifacts that might be deliberately or most of the time without knowing could produce.l

Because at the time end of the day … I could publish “something” … but years down if i am disproven my whole career is under water. I will be done. That’s what I always wanted to avoid. 

But not many get lucky and many don’t put a lot of thoughts into being careful and thorough due to pressure. I doubt the professor knew. But at the end … the professor will get the most of the criticism and career issues due to something like this.

What i wrote above is my own experiences and feelings. I have been in meetings where I have called out seemingly artificers like this. It’s laziness . My old post doc advisor hated me for it because it was always a guy in that lab that did it and i became that feminist who hated men. He ended messing my career so bad. So we can’t always do the right thing either,

text:
Immediate help  
0800 212121 Mental Health Uganda helpline (toll-free from any Ugandan phone). Counselling, first aid and referrals.  
999 or 112  Police / emergency if there is immediate physical danger.

Main public hospital  
Butabika National Referral Mental Hospital  
Plot 2, Kirombe-Butabika Road, Kampala (about 12 km east of the city centre).
24/7 emergency intake.  
Phone: +256 414 504 375  
Hospital site also lists 0800 211 306.  
Mulago National Referral Hospital’s psychiatric department also accepts emergencies.

Community and NGO options in Kampala  
StrongMinds Uganda  Free or low-cost group therapy for depression in communities, schools and health facilities (including Katwe). Works with government partners. https://t.co/zYHOGYLZEI  
GambaCare WhatsApp service matching people with verified Ugandan therapists (English, Luganda, Swahili). Free daily vent sessions plus paid therapy (typically ~UGX 50,000, Mobile Money). https://t.co/AewgJLTLu9  
Heart to Heart Spaces  Workshops, referrals and community support. +256 700 410 356, https://t.co/yS9aRCfNEu  
Safe Places Uganda Private outpatient clinic in Kyambogo (Plot 12, Lancaster Avenue) for mental health, neurology and addiction; residential site further out. +256 770 700944, https://t.co/wEWXqNCXuM  
You Belong Uganda and similar lived-experience programmes that support people with psychosis in the community and ease pressure on Butabika.

Other useful services  
Makerere University Hospital runs an Early Intervention Psychiatry clinic (assessment, therapy and follow-up, including for students).  
Private psychologists and lower-level health centres in Kampala also offer counselling; private session fees often start around UGX 60,000–120,000.

Public care at Butabika and government facilities is free or heavily subsidised, though the hospital is often overcrowded. Community programmes such as StrongMinds aim to bring support closer to where people live.
